docs.title: Question
docs.text: What does Daniel 8 establish (E/N), and how do the three readings compare?

docs.title: Study Plan Context
docs.text:
This is a COMPARE study reading the three perspective studies for Daniel 8: - dan3-11-HIST-daniel-8 - dan3-12-PRET-daniel-8 - dan3-13-FUT-daniel-8

Prior COMPARE conclusions providing accumulated context: - dan3-06-COMPARE-daniel-2 - dan3-10-COMPARE-daniel-7

Key adjudications from the plan (dan2-14-COMPARE): 1. mehem antecedent: grammar textbook evidence (GKC 135o, constructio ad sensum) -- does the 3mp suffix on two feminine antecedents resolve toward winds or horns? 2. gadal/yether progression: does the text REQUIRE the horn to exceed both named empires? 3. nitsdaq: forensic vindication vs. temple restoration -- lexical evidence (53/54 concordance distribution, LXX standard dikaioo) 4. 2300 full days vs. 1150 half-days: erev-boqer grammar (Gen 1 parallel vs. DOA formula) 5. 2300/1150 historical math test against the actual Antiochus period (~1105 days) 6. "Time of the end" (eth qets): what does the phrase require? (Danielic technical term, 5 occurrences)

docs.title: From Perspective Studies (Mandatory Reading)
docs.text:
dan3-11-HIST-daniel-8: - Question: How does historicism read Daniel 8, and what is the textual/grammatical basis for identifying the little horn as Rome? - Horn identity: Rome (pagan + papal) under one symbol. Classification: I-A(1) for most specifications; no E-tier for the identification itself (text does not name Rome). - Gadal/yether progression: Ram gadal (Hiphil, unmodified), goat gadal ad-meod (Hiphil + intensifier), horn gadal-yether (Qal + surplus). The stem shift from Hiphil to Qal signals organic/inherent growth. yether (H3499) = surplus/preeminence. HIST argues this mathematically eliminates Antiochus (~3M km2 vs. Persia ~5.5-8M km2 and Greece ~5.2M km2). - Az paniym exclusive construct chain: Only Deut 28:50 and Dan 8:23 -- ties the horn to the covenant-curse framework. - Nitsdaq (H6663 Niphal): The ONLY Niphal of tsadaq in the OT. Forensic, not ritual. Daniel deliberately chose tsadaq over taher (94x) and kaphar (102x). Old Greek preserves dikaiothesatai (forensic); Theodotion shifts to katharisthesetai. - Eth qets chain: Dan 8:17; 11:35; 11:40; 12:4; 12:9 -- terminates at bodily resurrection (Dan 12:2). Cannot be confined to Maccabean era. - Dan 8-9 connection: Gabriel returns (9:21-23) to explain the mar'eh (8:26-27). Shared vocabulary: pesha (8:12-13, 9:24), tsadaq root (8:14, 9:24), qodesh (8:14, 9:24). Chathak hapax (H2852, 9:24) = "cut off from" larger period. - Vocabulary bridges: pasha-anomos bridge (Dan 8:23 -> Isa 53:12 -> 2 Thess 2:8); tsadaq chain (Isa 53:11 yatsdiq -> Dan 8:14 nitsdaq -> Dan 12:3 matsdiqey); Rev 13:6 three-to-three correspondence with Dan 8:10-12. - Two-phase reading: ha-tamid VE ha-pesha (two definite-article nouns) = two sequential desolating systems under one horn symbol. - Specification-match tally: 0 E, 0 N, 18 I-A(1) [11 HIGH, 7 MED], 5 I-A(2) [all MED], 0 I-C. Average chain depth ~1.3. - Honest weaknesses: chathak is hapax; Rome identification is inference; mehem grammar is ambiguous; several specs also fit Antiochus; heavenly sanctuary identification relies on Hebrews typology.

dan3-12-PRET-daniel-8: - Question: How does preterism read Daniel 8, and what is the textual basis for identifying the little horn as Antiochus IV? - Horn identity: Antiochus IV Epiphanes. PRET's strongest argument: be-acharit malkutam (Dan 8:23) -- the -am suffix on malkut points back to the four Greek successor kingdoms (8:22), explicitly timestamping the horn's rise within the Hellenistic era. Classification: I-A(1) HIGH. - Dan 8/Dan 11 vocabulary correspondence: tamid, mirmah, shalvah, miqdash shared between Dan 8 and Dan 11:21-35 (near-consensus Antiochus context). BUT the parallel is thematic, not verbatim -- different verbs (rum Hophal vs. sur Hiphil), different desolation nouns (pesha vs. shiqquts). Classification: I-A(1) MED. - Directional match: South (Egypt), east (Persia/Parthia), pleasant land (Judea) match documented Antiochene campaigns. I-A(1) HIGH. - Activity matches: Tamid removed (I-A(1) HIGH), sanctuary desecrated (I-A(1) HIGH), host given by transgression (I-A(1) HIGH), truth cast to ground (I-A(1) MED), broken without hand = death by disease (I-A(1) HIGH). - 2300/1150 reading: Divides erev-boqer by 2 to get 1150 literal days. BUT ~1105 actual days (45-day shortfall, ~4%). I-A(2) LOW. - nitsdaq as temple restoration (Hanukkah): Depends on Theodotion's katharisthesetai rather than Hebrew/Old Greek forensic sense. I-B LOW -- competing E-LEX evidence. - gadal/yether as I-B: Antiochus geopolitically smaller than both named empires; PRET's shift to "theological greatness" lacks textual warrant. I-B LOW. - Specification-match tally: 14 specifications ranging from I-A(1) HIGH to I-B LOW. Two I-B items (gadal/yether and nitsdaq), both LOW. No E-tier for the Antiochus identification. - Honest weaknesses: gadal/yether progression (I-B), 2300/1150 arithmetic failure (45 days), eth qets chain to Dan 12:2 resurrection, nitsdaq forensic sense against ritual reading, three NT authors apply Daniel's imagery beyond Maccabean era, Dan 8/11 parallel is thematic not verbatim.

dan3-13-FUT-daniel-8: - Question: How does dispensationalist futurism read Daniel 8, and what is the textual basis for a type/antitype reading? - Horn identity: Antiochus IV as type, future Antichrist as antitype. FUT accepts Antiochus as historical fulfillment for many specifications but projects ultimate fulfillment to eschatological Antichrist. - NT convergence (FUT's strongest argument): Three witnesses apply Daniel's horn imagery to a post-Maccabean figure -- Jesus (Matt 24:15), Paul (2 Thess 2:3-8), John (Rev 13:1-7). Dense vocabulary parallels. I-A(1) HIGH. BUT Matt 24:15 has competing AD 70 reading (Luke 21:20 parallel), introducing I-B element. - Eth qets chain: Same as HIST -- extends vision to bodily resurrection. I-A(1) HIGH. FUT and HIST share this argument. - Type/antitype framework: 1 John 2:18 provides direct warrant ("antichrist shall come, even now are there many antichrists"). Multiple NT typological precedents (Rom 5:14, 1 Cor 5:7, Heb 8:5). BUT Daniel 8 itself contains NO dual-fulfillment textual marker. - Literal 2300 days: ~6.3 years in 360-day prophetic calendar, fitting within 7-year tribulation framework from Dan 9:27. I-C LOW. - Third Temple dependency: 2 Thess 2:4 naos -- but Paul uses naos metaphorically for church in 1 Cor 3:16-17, 2 Cor 6:16, Eph 2:21. I-C LOW. - Dan 8-9 connection as counter-evidence against FUT: Gabriel's return creates #4a SIS link between 2300 and 70 weeks. If 70 weeks = 490 years, 2300 must also be years. FUT must sever this link or argue independent prophecies. - Horn-split problem: FUT assigns Dan 7 horn to future Antichrist (from Rome) and Dan 8 horn to Antiochus (from Greece) -- but extensive vocabulary overlap across the two suggests one figure. - Specification-match tally: "Type" identifications at I-A(1) MED-HIGH; "antitype" identifications at I-A(2) (depend on type/antitype framework); distinctive FUT claims (literal 2300, Third Temple) at I-C LOW. FUT's strongest items are shared with HIST (eth qets, NT convergence). - Honest weaknesses: Type/antitype hermeneutic reads later theology back into text; no dual-fulfillment marker in Dan 8; Antiochus still fails yether even as type; literal 2300 faces Dan 8-9 connection; Third Temple is I-C; horn-split creates internal tension.

docs.title: From Prior COMPARE Studies (Accumulated Verdicts)
docs.text:
dan3-06-COMPARE-daniel-2: - E-tier items (12, all ALL): Babylon = head of gold; four sequential kingdoms; fourth = iron-crushing power; divided phase; mingling/non-cleaving; God's everlasting kingdom; stone without hands; ka-chadah simultaneous destruction; Dan 8:20 (Medo-Persia = one entity); Dan 8:21 (Greece); Dan 8:22 (four successor malkuyot); Dan 5:28. - N-tier items (6, all ALL): Medo-Persia = 2nd; Greece = 3rd; PRET Schema A eliminated by Dan 8:20; fourth follows Greece; stone divine origin; stone everlasting. - Fourth kingdom I-B resolution: Moderate toward Rome. Rome at I-A(1) HIGH vs. Greek successors at I-A(2) MED. Three constraints on PRET: batarakh succession language, gadal/yether scale, iron chain scope. - Stone timing I-B resolution: Moderate toward two-phase reading (inaugurated + future consummation). Matt 21:44 contains both present and future dimensions. - HIST aggregate: 2 E, 2 N, 6 I-A(1), 2 I-A(2). Average chain depth 1.25. 10 HIGH, 2 MED, 0 LOW. - PRET aggregate: 2 E, 2 I-A(1), 7 I-A(2), 1 I-A(3). Average chain depth 2.0. 3 HIGH, 7 MED, 2 LOW. - FUT aggregate: 2 E, 2 E+I-A(1), 2 I-A(1), 4 I-A(2), 2 I-A(2)+I-C. Average chain depth 1.75. 5 HIGH, 3 MED, 4 LOW. - Key constraining effects: Dan 8:20 eliminates PRET Schema A; ka-chadah constrains PRET stone timing; tselem chad (one image) constrains FUT gap thesis; "filled the whole earth" constrains inaugurated-only reading.

dan3-10-COMPARE-daniel-7: - E-tier items (19, all ALL): Four beasts = four kings; fourth beast = fourth kingdom; ten horns = ten kings + another displaces three; horn speaks against Most High; wears out saints (bela Pa'el = intensive ongoing); thinks to change times and law; saints delivered for 3.5 times; judgment set + books opened; Son of Man approaches Ancient of Days (three directional indicators); triple everlasting kingdom declaration; judgment removes horn's dominion; Dan 2:21 Haph'el shanah; Rev 13:5 verbal correspondence; mystery of iniquity already at work. - N-tier items (8, all ALL): Medo-Persia = 2nd; Greece = 3rd; fourth follows Greece; Haph'el shanah = horn usurps divine prerogative; iddan = year (Dan 4 precedent); bela Pa'el = intensive ongoing; Son of Man direction toward God; horn activities precede judgment. - I-B resolutions: PRET everlasting kingdom = Strong resolution against PRET (triple emphatic + messianic chain). PRET beast slain = Moderate against PRET (Seleucid empire continued ~100 years). FUT Dan 7:13 direction = Moderate (Aramaic indicates approach to God; NT adds earthward manifestation). - HIST aggregate: Average chain depth 1.6, 4 HIGH + 5 MED, 0 I-B, 0 I-C. - PRET aggregate: Average chain depth 2.25, 0 HIGH (for identification matches), 5 MED, 4 LOW, 2 I-B. - FUT aggregate: Average chain depth 1.7, 3 HIGH + 5 MED + 2 LOW, 1 I-B, 2 I-C LOW. - Key constraining effects: Triple "everlasting kingdom" constrains PRET; bela Pa'el semantics favor prolonged attrition (constrains PRET and FUT compressed periods); Dan 7:13 directional indicators constrain direct Second Coming reading; "already work" (E19) constrains exclusively-future FUT reading; "devour the whole earth" constrains PRET Seleucid identification. - Cumulative pattern confirmed: HIST has shallowest inference chain across Dan 2 and Dan 7. PRET carries highest chain depth and I-B tensions. FUT shares HIST's strong ground but adds I-C LOW framework dependencies.

docs.title: From Semantic Search (Additional)
docs.text:
daniel-8-great-progression: (score: 0.623) - Dedicated word study on the gadal/yether progression in Dan 8:4,8,9. - Key finding: yether (H3499) = excess/surplus/preeminence, requiring the horn to SURPASS both predecessors. - Stem shift: Hiphil (causative, ram/goat) to Qal (simple/inherent, horn) indicates organic growth. - Directional indicators (8:4,9) prove gadal in these verses refers to TERRITORIAL expansion, not personal pride (personal pride uses bilbav "in heart" modifier, as in 8:25). - Conclusion: yether linguistically excludes Antiochus and fits Rome alone.

sanc-25-daniel-8-14-vindicated: (score: 0.385) - Dedicated study on nitsdaq in Dan 8:14. - Key finding: nitsdaq is the ONLY Niphal of tsadaq in the entire OT -- a hapax form. Every other passive tsadaq is forensic/judicial. The root appears 41 times as a verb (54 KJV occurrences), always forensic. - The kaphar -> tsadaq progression: Lev 16:30 (kaphar -> taher = process), Dan 9:24 (kaphar -> tsedeq = process-to-result), Isa 53:11 (bearing iniquities -> yatsdiq), Rom 3:25-26 (hilasterion -> dikaios/dikaioo). The DOA is the process; nitsdaq announces the result (vindication). - Attack-question-vindication sequence: Dan 8:9-12 (fourfold attack) -> 8:13 (ad matay prophetic complaint) -> 8:14 (nitsdaq forensic answer). The four dimensions of vindication: God's people, God's authority, God's sanctuary/ministry, God's truth. - KJV "cleansed" is anomalous -- the only time tsadaq is translated with cleansing vocabulary in 54 occurrences.

dan-8-14-evening-mornings: (score: 0.331) - Relevant to the erev-boqer grammar adjudication. - Explores why Daniel uses "evening-morning" rather than yamim ("days") or DOA formula.

daniel-8-9-grammar-origin-little-horn / v2: (scores: 0.524/0.496) - Dedicated grammar studies on the mehem antecedent question. - Relevant to GKC 135o constructio ad sensum adjudication.

docs.title: EGW Writings
docs.text:
Score Refcode Key Content 0.865 PFF4 736.2 (Froom) "The exceeding great horn of Daniel 8 is Rome, both pagan and papal. (Not Antiochus Epiphanes, or Mohammedanism.)" 0.819 PFF3 363 (Froom) "Horn of Daniel 8 papal not Mohammedan" -- historical survey of interpretive positions 0.814 BHB 50.6 (Haskell) "Daniel was shown that the sanctuary would be cleansed at the end of the 2300 days, or in the autumn of 1844." 0.810 SYNPT 27.1 (Smith) "The Prophecy of Daniel 8:14 simply declares that at the end of the 2300 days the sanctuary shall be cleansed. The subject of the sanctuary thus becomes the central and controlling question." 0.811 SLWM 200.3 (EGW) "In the 8th chapter of Daniel is recorded a vision which was to extend to the cleansing of the sanctuary, and to continue 2300 days." Gabriel explains the vision reaches to "the last end of the indignation." 0.813 MRSH 21.1 (Miller) "490 years cannot be a part of six years, and of course the 2300 must be so many years; and if all the skeptics in Christendom... should try to make me believe that the vision in the 8th chapter of Daniel was fulfilled under Antiochus Epiphanes, I could not do it." Uses the Dan 8-9 connection as the linchpin argument. 0.823 Cuninghame "The vision shall be unto the time of the end... Consequently, the 2300 days of the vision must be prophetic days, used for years." Uses eth qets as evidence for day-year reading.

Claims to verify biblically: 1. The Dan 8 horn is Rome in both pagan and papal phases (not Antiochus) -- verify via gadal/yether progression, az paniym exclusivity, eth qets scope, and cross-vision consistency with Dan 2/7 fourth-kingdom evidence. 2. The 2300 erev-boqer are prophetic-day years, not literal days -- verify via Dan 8-9 Gabriel connection (mar'eh/biyn chain), chathak-70-week link, and erev-boqer grammar vs. yamim (Dan 12:11). 3. The sanctuary of Dan 8:14 is the heavenly sanctuary -- verify via Heb 8:1-2, 9:11-12 typological framework and qodesh (not miqdash) in 8:14 vs. mekhon miqdash in 8:11. 4. The eth qets argument: Gabriel's "time of the end" declaration proves the vision extends beyond Antiochus -- verify via the five-link eth qets chain (8:17; 11:35; 11:40; 12:4; 12:9) terminating at Dan 12:2 resurrection.

docs.title: Secrets Unsealed (Stephen Bohr)
docs.text:
Score Book Refcode Key Content 0.744 TLTT p. 37 "The Conniving Little Horn of Daniel 8" -- title reference 0.649 GPOT2V1 Lesson #14, p. 395 "Notes on Daniel 8: The Sanctuary Shall Be Cleansed" -- full lesson on Dan 8 0.598 GPOT2V1 Lesson #14, p. 450 Argues vindication and cleansing overlap: "The reputation of God and his people has been smeared by the little horn and a judicial proceeding in the heavenly sanctuary must set the record straight, must vindicate, must justify and must expunge or cleanse the false accusations." Links Dan 7:9-10 (judicial) to Dan 8:14 (sanctuary). 0.589 GPOT2V1 Lesson #14, p. 439 Notes the terminological shift: miqdash in Dan 8:11 vs. qodesh in Dan 8:14 -- argues this signals a shift from the physical sanctuary (attacked) to holiness/sacred things (vindicated). 0.574 GPOT2V1 Lesson #14, p. 443 "On the surface, it would appear that the best translation of Daniel 8:14 would be 'vindicated' or 'justified' rather than 'cleansed.' However, appearances can be deceiving and we need to beware of jumping to hasty conclusions before considering all the evidence."

Claims to verify biblically: 1. Dan 7:9-10 (judicial proceeding) parallels Dan 8:14 (sanctuary vindication) -- both describe the same heavenly judgment from different angles. Verify via shared vocabulary and structural correspondence. 2. The miqdash -> qodesh vocabulary shift (Dan 8:11 vs. 8:14) is significant: miqdash = the physical location attacked; qodesh = holiness/sacred things vindicated. Verify via lexical analysis of the two terms in Daniel. 3. Vindication includes both forensic justification AND cleansing of false accusations -- the two concepts overlap rather than exclude each other. Verify via the tsadaq semantic field and the attack-question-answer structure of Dan 8:9-14.

docs.text:
• 3 perspective studies read with full specification-match tallies, vocabulary chains, and honest weaknesses extracted

  • Key leads for the COMPARE study:
  • The six adjudication questions from the plan are each well-supported by prior study data. The gadal/yether and nitsdaq adjudications have dedicated prior word studies. The mehem grammar has two prior grammar studies. The erev-boqer question has a dedicated prior study. The eth qets chain and 2300/1150 math test are well-documented in all three perspective studies.

Daniel 8 COMPARE should test whether this pattern holds.

docs.title: Question
docs.text: What does Daniel 8 establish (E/N), and how do the three readings (HIST/PRET/FUT) compare?

docs.title: HORN
docs.text:
• Used to contain the anointing oil: 1SA 16:1; 1KI 1:39
  • Used for a trumpet (See TRUMPET)
  • FIGURATIVE
  • Of divine protection: 2SA 22:3
  • Of power: 1KI 22:11; PSA 89:24; 92:10; 132:17
  • SYMBOLICAL: DAN 7:7-24; 8:3-9,20; AMO 6:13; MIC 4:13; HAB 3:4; ZEC 1:18-21; REV 5:6; 12:3; 13:1,11; 17:3-16

Key observation: Horn is consistently a symbol of power in prophetic/apocalyptic literature. Daniel 7-8 and Revelation use horn symbolism extensively for political/religious powers.

docs.title: SANCTUARY
docs.text:
• (The Holy of Holies)
  • In the tabernacle: HEB 9:2
  • Divine dwelling place: EXO 25:8
  • Reverence for: LEV 19:30; 26:2
  • In the charge of high priest: EXO 27:21; LEV 24:3; NUM 18:5
  • The Holy Place in the temple: LAM 2:7,20; EZK 42:20
  • FIGURATIVE: EZK 11:16
  • Symbolical: HEB 8:2,5

Key observation: Nave's includes both earthly and heavenly/symbolical sanctuary. HEB 8:2,5 explicitly identifies a heavenly sanctuary. The question for Dan 8:14 is whether qodesh refers to the earthly Jerusalem temple or the heavenly.

docs.title: COUNTENANCE
docs.text:
• Angry: PRO 25:23
  • Cheerful: JOB 29:24; PSA 4:6; 21:6; 44:3; PRO 15:13; 27:17
  • Fierce: DEU 28:50; DAN 8:23 -- THE ONLY TWO ENTRIES
  • Guilty: GEN 4:5; ISA 3:9
  • Health indicated in: PSA 42:11; 43:5
  • Sad: 1SA 1:18; NEH 2:2,3; ECC 7:3; EZK 27:35; DAN 1:15; 5:6
  • Transfigured: EXO 34:29-35; 2CO 3:7,13; LUK 9:29

Key observation: Under "Fierce" countenance, Nave's lists ONLY two verses: Deut 28:50 and Dan 8:23. This confirms the exclusive intertextual link between the covenant curse nation (Deut 28) and the Daniel 8 horn power. The az-paniym construct occurs nowhere else.

docs.title: JUSTICE
docs.text:
• EXO 23:1-3,6-8; LEV 19:13-15; DEU 16:18-20; 25:1-4; EZR 7:26
  • PSA 72:1,2; 82:2-4; PRO 17:15,26; 18:5,17; 20:8; 22:27; 24:23; 28:21; 29:26
  • ECC 3:16,17; 5:8; 7:7; ISA 1:17; 56:1; 59:14,15; JER 22:1-4
  • LAM 3:35,36; AMO 5:7,11,12; MIC 7:3; HAB 1:4; ZEC 8:16
  • MAT 5:23; 12:7; JHN 7:24,51; 1CO 13:6

Key observation: The forensic/legal sense of justice is prominent. DEU 25:1 ("they shall justify the righteous and condemn the wicked") uses the same tsadaq root as Dan 8:14. PRO 17:15 ("He that justifieth the wicked, and he that condemneth the just, even they both are abomination to the LORD") confirms the forensic declarative sense.

docs.title: SACRILEGE
docs.text:
• (Profaning holy things)
  • Forbidden: LEV 19:8; 1CO 3:17; TIT 1:11; 1PE 5:2
  • Instances: Nadab/Abihu (LEV 10:1-7); Uzzah (2SA 6:6,7); Uzziah (2CH 26:16-21); Korah (NUM 16:40); Beth-shemesh (1SA 6:19); Ahaz (2CH 28:24); Money-changers (MAT 21:12,13); Profaning Lord's Supper (1CO 11:29)

Key observation: Profaning holy things is the category of the horn's attack in Dan 8:11-13 -- against the sanctuary, the tamid, and the qodesh. The response in Dan 8:14 (nitsdaq qodesh) addresses this profanation with forensic vindication.

docs.title: COVENANT
docs.text:
• Sacred: JOS 9:18-21; GAL 3:15
  • Binding: JOS 9:18-20; JER 34:8-21; EZK 17:14-18
  • Blood of: EXO 24:8
  • OF GOD WITH MEN: Everlasting (GEN 8:20-22; 9:1-17; PSA 105:8,10; ISA 54:10; 61:8)
  • God faithful to: LEV 26:44,45; DEU 4:31; 7:8,9
  • Punishments for breaking of: LEV 26:25-46
  • To be confirmed: DAN 9:27
  • THE SECOND COVENANT: JER 31:31-34; HEB 8:4-13; 12:18-24; 13:20

Key observation: Deut 28 is covenant-curse language. The az-paniym nation of Deut 28:50 is a covenant judgment -- a nation sent by God as punishment for covenant-breaking. Dan 8:23's use of the same construct chain ties the horn power to covenant-curse execution.

docs.title: PROPHECY
docs.text:
• Inspired: ISA 28:22; LUK 1:70; 2TI 3:16; 2PE 1:21
  • Sure fulfillment of: EZK 12:22-25,28; HAB 2:3; MAT 5:18; 24:35; ACT 13:27,29
  • Of apostasy: 1JN 2:18; Jude 1:17,18
  • OLD TESTAMENT MESSIANIC PASSAGES QUOTED IN THE NT (extensive list including):
  • ISA 9:7 with DAN 7:14,27 with LUK 1:32,33
  • ISA 53:1-12 with multiple NT citations
  • DAN 7:14,27 linked to everlasting kingdom

Key observation: Daniel's prophecies are recognized in the NT as still-relevant. Jesus cites Daniel directly (Matt 24:15). The PROPHECY topic links Dan 7:14,27 to Isa 9:7 and Luk 1:32,33, confirming eschatological scope.

docs.title: Daniel 8:1
docs.text: In the third year of the reign of king Belshazzar a vision appeared unto me, even unto me Daniel, after that which appeared unto me at the first.

docs.title: Daniel 8:2
docs.text: And I saw in a vision; and it came to pass, when I saw, that I was at Shushan in the palace, which is in the province of Elam; and I saw in a vision, and I was by the river of Ulai.

docs.title: Daniel 8:3
docs.text: Then I lifted up mine eyes, and saw, and, behold, there stood before the river a ram which had two horns: and the two horns were high; but one was higher than the other, and the higher came up last.

docs.title: Daniel 8:4
docs.text: I saw the ram pushing westward, and northward, and southward; so that no beasts might stand before him, neither was there any that could deliver out of his hand; but he did according to his will, and became great.

docs.title: Daniel 8:5
docs.text: And as I was considering, behold, an he goat came from the west on the face of the whole earth, and touched not the ground: and the goat had a notable horn between his eyes.

docs.title: Daniel 8:6
docs.text: And he came to the ram that had two horns, which I had seen standing before the river, and ran unto him in the fury of his power.

docs.title: Daniel 8:7
docs.text: And I saw him come close unto the ram, and he was moved with choler against him, and smote the ram, and brake his two horns: and there was no power in the ram to stand before him, but he cast him down to the ground, and stamped upon him: and there was none that could deliver the ram out of his hand.

docs.title: Daniel 8:8
docs.text: Therefore the he goat waxed very great: and when he was strong, the great horn was broken; and for it came up four notable ones toward the four winds of heaven.

docs.title: Daniel 8:9
docs.text: And out of one of them came forth a little horn, which waxed exceeding great, toward the south, and toward the east, and toward the pleasant land.

docs.title: Daniel 8:10
docs.text: And it waxed great, even to the host of heaven; and it cast down some of the host and of the stars to the ground, and stamped upon them.

docs.title: Daniel 8:11
docs.text: Yea, he magnified himself even to the prince of the host, and by him the daily sacrifice was taken away, and the place of his sanctuary was cast down.

docs.title: Daniel 8:12
docs.text: And an host was given him against the daily sacrifice by reason of transgression, and it cast down the truth to the ground; and it practised, and prospered.

docs.title: Daniel 8:13
docs.text: Then I heard one saint speaking, and another saint said unto that certain saint which spake, How long shall be the vision concerning the daily sacrifice, and the transgression of desolation, to give both the sanctuary and the host to be trodden under foot?

docs.title: Daniel 8:14
docs.text: And he said unto me, Unto two thousand and three hundred days; then shall the sanctuary be cleansed.

docs.title: Daniel 8:15
docs.text: And it came to pass, when I, even I Daniel, had seen the vision, and sought for the meaning, then, behold, there stood before me as the appearance of a man.

docs.title: Daniel 8:16

docs.title: Daniel 8:17
docs.text: So he came near where I stood: and when he came, I was afraid, and fell upon my face: but he said unto me, Understand, O son of man: for at the time of the end shall be the vision.

docs.title: Daniel 8:18
docs.text: Now as he was speaking with me, I was in a deep sleep on my face toward the ground: but he touched me, and set me upright.

docs.title: Daniel 8:19

docs.title: Daniel 8:20

docs.title: Daniel 8:21

docs.title: Daniel 7:1-6 (Beasts 1-3)
docs.text: 7:1 In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon Daniel had a dream and visions of his head upon his bed: then he wrote the dream, and told the sum of the matters. 7:2 Daniel spake and said, I saw in my vision by night, and, behold, the four winds of the heaven strove upon the great sea. 7:3 And four great beasts came up from the sea, diverse one from another. 7:4 The first was like a lion, and had eagle's wings... 7:5 And behold another beast, a second, like to a bear... 7:6 After this I beheld, and lo another, like a leopard, which had upon the back of it four wings of a fowl; the beast had also four heads; and dominion was given to it.

docs.title: Daniel 7:7-8 (Fourth Beast and Little Horn)
docs.text: 7:7 After this I saw in the night visions, and behold a fourth beast, dreadful and terrible, and strong exceedingly; and it had great iron teeth: it devoured and brake in pieces, and stamped the residue with the feet of it: and it was diverse from all the beasts that were before it; and it had ten horns. 7:8 I considered the horns, and, behold, there came up among them another little horn, before whom there were three of the first horns plucked up by the roots: and, behold, in this horn were eyes like the eyes of man, and a mouth speaking great things.

docs.title: Daniel 7:9-14 (Judgment Scene and Son of Man)
docs.text: 7:9 I beheld till the thrones were cast down, and the Ancient of days did sit, whose garment was white as snow, and the hair of his head like the pure wool: his throne was like the fiery flame, and his wheels as burning fire. 7:10 A fiery stream issued and came forth from before him: thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened. 7:11 I beheld then because of the voice of the great words which the horn spake: I beheld even till the beast was slain, and his body destroyed, and given to the burning flame. 7:12 As concerning the rest of the beasts, they had their dominion taken away: yet their lives were prolonged for a season and time. 7:13 I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him. 7:14 And there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all people, nations, and languages, should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.

docs.title: Daniel 7:15-28 (Interpretation)
docs.text: 7:17 These great beasts, which are four, are four kings, which shall arise out of the earth. 7:18 But the saints of the most High shall take the kingdom, and possess the kingdom for ever, even for ever and ever. 7:21 I beheld, and the same horn made war with the saints, and prevailed against them; 7:22 Until the Ancient of days came, and judgment was given to the saints of the most High; and the time came that the saints possessed the kingdom. 7:23 Thus he said, The fourth beast shall be the fourth kingdom upon earth, which shall be diverse from all kingdoms, and shall devour the whole earth, and shall tread it down, and break it in pieces. 7:24 And the ten horns out of this kingdom are ten kings that shall arise: and another shall rise after them; and he shall be diverse from the first, and he shall subdue three kings. 7:25 And he shall speak great words against the most High, and shall wear out the saints of the most High, and think to change times and laws: and they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of time. 7:26 But the judgment shall sit, and they shall take away his dominion, to consume and to destroy it unto the end. 7:27 And the kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the most High, whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey him. 7:28 Hitherto is the end of the matter. As for me Daniel, my cogitations much troubled me, and my countenance changed in me: but I kept the matter in my heart.

docs.title: Dan 8-9 Connection: Daniel 9:20-27
docs.text:
9:20 And whiles I was speaking, and praying, and confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel, and presenting my supplication before the LORD my God for the holy mountain of my God; 9:21 Yea, whiles I was speaking in prayer, even the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, being caused to fly swiftly, touched me about the time of the evening oblation. 9:22 And he informed me, and talked with me, and said, O Daniel, I am now come forth to give thee skill and understanding. 9:23 At the beginning of thy supplications the commandment came forth, and I am come to shew thee; for thou art greatly beloved: therefore understand the matter, and consider the vision. 9:24 Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy. 9:25 Know therefore and understand, that from the going forth of the commandment to restore and to build Jerusalem unto the Messiah the Prince shall be seven weeks, and threescore and two weeks: the street shall be built again, and the wall, even in troublous times. 9:26 And after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself: and the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary; and the end thereof shall be with a flood, and unto the end of the war desolations are determined. 9:27 And he shall confirm the covenant with many for one week: and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease, and for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate, even until the consummation, and that determined shall be poured upon the desolate.

Connection notes: Gabriel (9:21) = same Gabriel from Dan 8:16. "The vision at the beginning" (9:21) = the Dan 8 vision. "Understand the matter, and consider the vision" (9:23) = the vision Daniel did not understand (8:27). Shared vocabulary: pesha (8:12,13 / 9:24), chazon (8:1,2,13,15,17,26 / 9:24), qodesh (8:13,14 / 9:24,26), tsedeq/tsadaq (8:14 / 9:24).

docs.title: Eth Qets Chain: Daniel 12:1-13
docs.text:
12:1 And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book. 12:2 And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt. 12:3 And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever. 12:4 But thou, O Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the time of the end: many shall run to and fro, and knowledge shall be increased. 12:5 Then I Daniel looked, and, behold, there stood other two, the one on this side of the bank of the river, and the other on that side of the bank of the river. 12:6 And one said to the man clothed in linen, which was upon the waters of the river, How long shall it be to the end of these wonders? 12:7 And I heard the man clothed in linen, which was upon the waters of the river, when he held up his right hand and his left hand unto heaven, and sware by him that liveth for ever that it shall be for a time, times, and an half; and when he shall have accomplished to scatter the power of the holy people, all these things shall be finished. 12:8 And I heard, but I understood not: then said I, O my Lord, what shall be the end of these things? 12:9 And he said, Go thy way, Daniel: for the words are closed up and sealed till the time of the end. 12:10 Many shall be purified, and made white, and tried; but the wicked shall do wickedly: and none of the wicked shall understand; but the wise shall understand. 12:11 And from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days. 12:12 Blessed is he that waiteth, and cometh to the thousand three hundred and five and thirty days. 12:13 But go thou thy way till the end be: for thou shalt rest, and stand in thy lot at the end of the days.

Eth qets chain through Daniel: 8:17 (le-eth qets hahazon) -> 8:19 (le-mo'ed qets) -> 11:35 (ad-eth qets) -> 11:40 (be-eth qets) -> 12:4 (ad-eth qets) -> 12:9 (ad-eth qets) -> 12:13 (la-qets... le-qets hayyamim). The chain terminates at 12:2 (bodily resurrection) and 12:13 (Daniel's own resurrection).

docs.title: Erev-Boqer Creation Formula: Genesis 1:1-8,13,19,23,31
docs.text:
1:1 In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth. 1:5 And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. And the evening and the morning were the first day. 1:8 And God called the firmament Heaven. And the evening and the morning were the second day. 1:13 And the evening and the morning were the third day. 1:19 And the evening and the morning were the fourth day. 1:23 And the evening and the morning were the fifth day. 1:31 And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good. And the evening and the morning were the sixth day.

Pattern: "va-yehi erev va-yehi boqer yom X" -- evening + morning = one complete day. This formula is the creation-day measure. Dan 8:14 uses "erev boqer" (evening morning) as a compound unit, and Dan 8:26 confirms with "mar'eh ha-erev ve-ha-boqer" (vision of the evening and the morning).

docs.title: Covenant Curse: Deuteronomy 28:45-53
docs.text:
28:45 Moreover all these curses shall come upon thee, and shall pursue thee, and overtake thee, till thou be destroyed; because thou hearkenedst not unto the voice of the LORD thy God, to keep his commandments and his statutes which he commanded thee: 28:48 Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the LORD shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things: and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee. 28:49 The LORD shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth; a nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand; 28:50 A nation of fierce countenance, which shall not regard the person of the old, nor shew favour to the young: 28:51 And he shall eat the fruit of thy cattle, and the fruit of thy land, until thou be destroyed... 28:52 And he shall besiege thee in all thy gates, until thy high and fenced walls come down... 28:53 And thou shalt eat the fruit of thine own body...

Key verse: Deut 28:50 = goy az-paniym ("nation of fierce countenance"). Dan 8:23 = melek az-paniym ("king of fierce countenance"). These are the ONLY two occurrences of the az-paniym construct in the entire OT (confirmed by Nave's COUNTENANCE entry). This exclusive intertextual link ties the Dan 8 horn to the covenant-curse tradition.

docs.title: Tamid Sacrifice Formula: Numbers 28:1-10
docs.text:
28:1 And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying, 28:2 Command the children of Israel, and say unto them, My offering, and my bread for my sacrifices made by fire, for a sweet savour unto me, shall ye observe to offer unto me in their due season. 28:3 And thou shalt say unto them, This is the offering made by fire which ye shall offer unto the LORD; two lambs of the first year without spot day by day, for a continual burnt offering. 28:4 The one lamb shalt thou offer in the morning, and the other lamb shalt thou offer at even; 28:5 And a tenth part of an ephah of flour for a meat offering... 28:6 It is a continual burnt offering, which was ordained in mount Sinai for a sweet savour... 28:8 And the other lamb shalt thou offer at even...

Key observation: The tamid (continual) offering consisted of TWO daily sacrifices: one morning (boqer), one evening (erev). If Dan 8:14's "erev boqer" refers to the tamid sacrifices, then 2300 erev-boqer = 1150 days (2 per day). But if erev-boqer follows the creation-day formula (Gen 1), then 2300 erev-boqer = 2300 full days. The Hebrew grammar in Dan 8:14 favors the creation-formula reading (see parsing notes).

docs.title: Forensic Righteousness Chain: Isaiah 53:10-12
docs.text:
53:10 Yet it pleased the LORD to bruise him; he hath put him to grief: when thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin, he shall see his seed, he shall prolong his days, and the pleasure of the LORD shall prosper in his hand. 53:11 He shall see of the travail of his soul, and shall be satisfied: by his knowledge shall my righteous servant justify many; for he shall bear their iniquities. 53:12 Therefore will I divide him a portion with the great, and he shall divide the spoil with the strong; because he hath poured out his soul unto death: and he was numbered with the transgressors; and he bare the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors.

Key verse: Isa 53:11 uses yatsdiq (Hiphil of tsadaq) = "shall justify." The mechanism: bearing iniquities produces justification/vindication. Same tsadaq root as Dan 8:14 (nitsdaq, Niphal). The forensic chain: Isa 53:11 (yatsdiq = justify many by bearing sin) -> Dan 9:24 (tsedeq olamim = bring in everlasting righteousness) -> Dan 8:14 (nitsdaq qodesh = the sanctuary/holiness is vindicated).

docs.title: Day of Atonement: Leviticus 16:29-34
docs.text:
16:29 And this shall be a statute for ever unto you: that in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, ye shall afflict your souls, and do no work at all... 16:30 For on that day shall the priest make an atonement for you, to cleanse you, that ye may be clean from all your sins before the LORD. 16:31 It shall be a sabbath of rest unto you, and ye shall afflict your souls, by a statute for ever. 16:33 And he shall make an atonement for the holy sanctuary, and he shall make an atonement for the tabernacle of the congregation, and for the altar, and he shall make an atonement for the priests, and for all the people of the congregation. 16:34 And this shall be an everlasting statute unto you, to make an atonement for the children of Israel for all their sins once a year.

Key observation: The DOA uses kaphar (atonement) producing taher (cleansing). Dan 8:14 does NOT use kaphar or taher -- it uses tsadaq (forensic vindication). Daniel had both words available but chose a different one, signaling a different concept than ritual cleansing.

docs.title: Heavenly Sanctuary: Hebrews 8:1-6
docs.text: 8:1 Now of the things which we have spoken this is the sum: We have such an high priest, who is set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens; 8:2 A minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man. 8:3 For every high priest is ordained to offer gifts and sacrifices... 8:4 For if he were on earth, he should not be a priest... 8:5 Who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See, saith he, that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount. 8:6 But now hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises.

docs.title: Hebrews 9:11-14,23-24
docs.text:
9:11 But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building; 9:12 Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us. 9:23 It was therefore necessary that the patterns of things in the heavens should be purified with these; but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these. 9:24 For Christ is not entered into the holy places made with hands, which are the figures of the true; but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us:

Key observation: Hebrews explicitly teaches: (1) there is a heavenly sanctuary (8:2); (2) the earthly was a pattern/shadow of the heavenly (8:5, 9:23-24); (3) heavenly things need purification (9:23); (4) Christ ministers in the heavenly sanctuary (9:24).

docs.title: 1 John 2:18
docs.text:
Little children, it is the last time: and as ye have heard that antichrist shall come, even now are there many antichrists; whereby we know that it is the last time.

NT convergence summary: Three independent NT witnesses apply Daniel's horn language beyond Antiochus: 1. Jesus (Matt 24:15) -- cites Daniel's abomination of desolation as still future (post-Maccabean) 2. Paul (2 Thess 2:3-8) -- describes man of sin who exalts himself above God, sits in temple, destroyed at Christ's coming (not Maccabean era) 3. John (Rev 13:1-7) -- beast with horn imagery, mouth speaking great things (Dan 7:8/8:25), war against saints (Dan 7:21/8:24), power over nations

docs.title: Isaiah 43:9,26 (tsadaq forensic usage)
docs.text:
43:9 Let all the nations be gathered together, and let the people be assembled: who among them can declare this, and shew us former things? let them bring forth their witnesses, that they may be justified: or let them hear, and say, It is truth. 43:26 Put me in remembrance: let us plead together: declare thou, that thou mayest be justified.

Key observation: In both verses, tsadaq appears in a courtroom/forensic context (witnesses, pleading, declaring). The consistent forensic usage supports reading Dan 8:14's nitsdaq as forensic vindication rather than ritual cleansing.
