docs.title: Daniel's Four Visions: The Historicist Case in Plain English
A Plain-English Summary
docs.text:
Daniel contains four separate visions — chapters 2, 7, 8–9, and 10–12 — each covering the same sweep of history from Babylon to the end of time, with each vision adding more detail than the one before it. The historicist reading is the view that these visions trace an unbroken sequence of world powers: Babylon, Medo-Persia, Greece, and Rome, followed by a religious-political power that arises from within Rome's territory and dominates for a period described symbolically as 1,260 years. Three of the four kingdoms are named inside Daniel's own text, and the fourth follows in a chain the text describes as having no gaps. The underlying claim of this reading is that Daniel's prophecies are not cryptic references to events that were already past when he wrote, nor predictions of a future anti-christ who will appear in a seven-year tribulation at the end of history — but a continuous narrative stretching from the prophet's day through the present age and into the final judgment.

This summary explains the main findings of the full technical study, in the order the Bible presents them.

docs.title: The Theological Starting Point: God Controls History
docs.text:
Before any prophetic symbol is interpreted, Daniel's book establishes one axiom through repeated testimony. Three foreign monarchs across two empires confess the same truth:

"He changeth the times and the seasons: he removeth kings, and setteth up kings." — Daniel 2:21

The Aramaic verbs here are continuous participles — ongoing, habitual divine action, not a one-time statement. Nebuchadnezzar after his humiliation, Belshazzar's hall through Daniel's lips, Darius the Mede in his decree — all three confirm the same sovereignty. This is the theological ground on which the four-kingdom sequence stands: kingdom succession is not random history but divinely ordered progression. It is predictable through prophecy precisely because God directs it.

One detail from this foundation proves structurally important later. The Aramaic root that describes God legitimately changing times and seasons in Daniel 2:21 is the same root that appears in Daniel 7:25, where a future power "thinks to change times and law." What God does, the horn presumes to do. The conflict Daniel describes is a contest over sovereignty.

docs.title: Daniel 2: The Image and the Four Kingdoms
docs.text:
The statue Nebuchadnezzar saw — gold head, silver chest, bronze belly, iron legs, iron-clay feet — represents four successive kingdoms. The first is named directly:

"Thou art this head of gold." — Daniel 2:38

The second is named in the same book: "PERES; Thy kingdom is divided, and given to the Medes and Persians" (Daniel 5:28), and again in chapter 8: "the ram which thou sawest having two horns are the kings of Media and Persia" (Daniel 8:20). The third is named: "the rough goat is the king of Grecia" (Daniel 8:21). Three of four kingdoms identified by the Bible's own text. The fourth follows in a chain the text calls unbroken — "and after thee," "and another third kingdom," with no gap language permitted between them.

The iron legs are "strong as iron," and the verb the text uses for iron's crushing action (d'qaq, "breaking in pieces") reappears in Daniel 7 at the same structural position — the fourth beast with iron teeth. This vocabulary link is one of sixteen word-chains that bind Daniel's vision cycles together.

The stone that strikes the image is "cut out without hands" and destroys all the metals simultaneously:

"Then was the iron, the clay, the brass, the silver, and the gold, broken to pieces together, and became like the chaff of the summer threshingfloors." — Daniel 2:35

The word "together" is the Aramaic ka-chadah — simultaneous destruction. This requirement constrains when the stone arrives: all four metals must still be present at that moment in some institutional form. The stone kingdom then becomes permanent:

"And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed: and the kingdom shall not be left to other people, but it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever." — Daniel 2:44

The divided phase — iron mixed with clay — represents a transformation within the fourth kingdom rather than a fifth. The iron vocabulary continues, but something alien is mixed in. Daniel 2:43 states plainly: "they shall not cleave one to another, even as iron is not mixed with clay." This prediction has been tested across fifteen centuries by Charlemagne, Napoleon, Hitler, and the European Union — none achieved permanent reunification of the old Roman territory.

docs.title: Daniel 7: The Little Horn, the Judgment, and the Kingdom
docs.text:
Daniel 7 revisits the same four-kingdom sequence but with critical additions: a small horn that arises from the fourth beast and dominates for a prophetic period of time, and a heavenly court that convenes before the eternal kingdom is given.

The four beasts match the four metals by their structural position and by the iron link — the fourth beast has "great iron teeth" (Daniel 7:7), the same metal at the same position. The angel confirms: "these great beasts, which are four, are four kings" (Daniel 7:17).

From the fourth beast's ten horns there arises a little horn with nine specific characteristics. It comes up after the ten, displaces three of them, is diverse from the others, has eyes like a man, and speaks with a mouth making great claims. Then:

"And he shall speak great words against the most High, and shall wear out the saints of the most High, and think to change times and laws: and they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of time." — Daniel 7:25

Several words here deserve close attention. The word translated "wear out" (bela in Aramaic) appears nowhere else in the Bible in this form — it is a hapax legomenon, an intensive stem meaning sustained grinding attrition, like a garment slowly wearing through. This describes not a sudden assault but a centuries-long campaign. The phrase "think to change times and laws" uses the singular emphatic "THE law" (dat), and the word for times is zimnin — appointed times. The convergence of these terms points to the only commandment that is simultaneously both a law and a time.

The heavenly judgment scene is the most distinctive element of Daniel 7:

"I beheld till the thrones were cast down, and the Ancient of days did sit, whose garment was white as snow, and the hair of his head like the pure wool: his throne was like the fiery flame, and his wheels as burning fire. A fiery stream issued and came forth from before him: thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened." — Daniel 7:9–10

The Aramaic is precise here: the thrones are "set/placed" (passive), not thrown down. The Son of Man comes "to" the Ancient of Days — he moves toward God in heaven, not downward to earth. The prepositions matter. This is a presentation and investiture in heaven, distinct from the Second Coming, where Acts 1:11 and 1 Thessalonians 4:16 describe descent from heaven. The judgment scene precedes the giving of the eternal kingdom; the Second Coming follows after.

The Book of Revelation confirms the connection. Nine elements of Daniel 7:9–14 reappear in Revelation 4–5: the throne, the seated Judge, white garments, fire from the throne, the identical myriads formula, books, the Lamb approaching the throne, authority given, universal worship. And Revelation 13:5 quotes Daniel 7:8 almost word for word from the Greek translation: "a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies."

docs.title: Daniel 8: The Surpassing Horn and the Sanctuary
docs.text:
Daniel 8 narrows the focus to Medo-Persia and Greece, both named by the angel, and then introduces a horn that surpasses both. The text tracks the horn's growth through a three-stage escalation: the ram "became great," the goat "waxed very great," and then the horn:

"And out of one of them came forth a little horn, which waxed exceeding great, toward the south, and toward the east, and toward the pleasant land." — Daniel 8:9

The Hebrew word translated "exceeding" here is yether — surplus, excess, preeminence. The horn must surpass both named empires in scope. This is not an interpretation but a mathematical constraint the text sets up. Any identification smaller in geographic scope than Medo-Persia or Greece fails the test the text itself establishes.

The horn "stands against the Prince of the host" (Daniel 8:11), removes the "daily" (tamid), and casts truth to the ground. Then Daniel hears a question and answer:

"And he said unto me, Unto two thousand and three hundred days; then shall the sanctuary be cleansed." — Daniel 8:14

The verb translated "cleansed" is nitsdaq — and it is the only occurrence in the entire Old Testament of this verb (tsadaq) in this passive form. Every related occurrence of tsadaq in passive contexts carries a forensic, judicial meaning: justification, vindication in a courtroom. Daniel had other words available if physical cleansing were meant (taher appears ninety-four times; kaphar appears a hundred and two times). The word chosen is the word for judicial vindication. The sanctuary is not merely cleaned — it is vindicated before a court.

Daniel 8:23 uses another exclusive construction: "a king of fierce countenance." This exact pairing of words appears in only two places in the entire Old Testament — here, and in Deuteronomy 28:50, where Moses describes the agent of the covenant curse. The link identifies Daniel 8's horn as the power Moses prophesied would come upon Israel for covenant breaking.

docs.title: Daniel 8–9: Two Visions as One Unit
docs.text:
Daniel 8 ends with Daniel still confused about the vision. Gabriel had been sent to explain it but stopped after explaining the ram and goat. When he returns in Daniel 9, he uses the identical grammatical construction he used in 8:16: the same verb form, the same object, the same speaker and recipient. The text is signaling that Gabriel is finishing what he started. Daniel 8 and 9 form one continuous interpretive unit.

Daniel 9:24 opens the second half of Gabriel's explanation:

"Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy." — Daniel 9:24

The word "determined" translates chathak — a hapax legomenon whose primary meaning in the lexicon is "to cut off." Daniel's normal word for "determine" (charats) appears just three verses later, in 9:26 and 9:27. The deliberate choice of a different, rarer word with a "cutting" meaning signals that the seventy weeks are cut off from a larger period — the 2,300-day period of Daniel 8:14.

The six purposes of Daniel 9:24 match the Day of Atonement sacrificial vocabulary of Leviticus 16:21 — the same three Hebrew roots for transgression, sin, and iniquity. Gabriel is describing a fulfillment of the Day of Atonement on a cosmic scale.

The seventy-week prophecy then runs through Messiah's appearance, his being "cut off," and the confirmation of the covenant:

"And after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself." — Daniel 9:26

"And he shall confirm the covenant with many for one week: and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease." — Daniel 9:27

The word "confirm" here is gabar — to strengthen an existing covenant — not karath, which means to cut a new one. Romans 15:8 uses the Greek equivalent (bebaioo, "confirm") when describing Christ confirming "the promises made unto the fathers." The covenant being strengthened is the one already given to Abraham.

Applied with the day-year principle and a starting point of 457 BC (the decree of Artaxerxes in Ezra 7), the sixty-nine weeks reach AD 27 — the beginning of Jesus' public ministry. Mark records the declaration at that moment: "The time is fulfilled" (Mark 1:15).

docs.title: The Day-Year Principle
docs.text:
The historicist reading applies a day-for-a-year scale to Daniel's prophetic time periods. This is not an assumption imported from outside the text. The Bible states the principle directly in two places:

"After the number of the days in which ye searched the land, even forty days, each day for a year, shall ye bear your iniquities, even forty years." — Numbers 14:34

"I have appointed thee each day for a year." — Ezekiel 4:6

Both passages use an identical Hebrew formula. Beyond these direct declarations, Daniel's own text gives additional signals. In Daniel 10:2–3, when Daniel mourns for literal weeks, he adds the word yamim (days) as a qualifier — "three full weeks." In Daniel 9:24 and 7:25, no such qualifier appears. Daniel 4:16 uses the Aramaic word iddan for the "seven times" of Nebuchadnezzar's madness — a period universally understood to mean seven years. The same word (iddan) appears in Daniel 7:25 for the little horn's period of dominance.

The sealing command in Daniel 8:26 also presses in this direction:

"Shut thou up the vision; for it shall be for many days."

If 2,300 meant 2,300 literal days (roughly six and a third years), Daniel himself would have lived to see the fulfillment, and no sealing would have been necessary. Daniel's reaction — the same word that describes the sanctuary's "desolation" — fits a man who glimpsed millennia of conflict, not years.

Seven separate time expressions across Daniel and Revelation — in three languages, across two books — yield the same mathematical result: 1,260 (time, times, and half a time; forty-two months; 1,260 days; a time, times, and half a time in Daniel 12:7). The consistency across these independent expressions is itself structural evidence.

docs.title: Daniel 10–12: The Detailed Narrative
docs.text:
Daniel 10:1 reports that Daniel "understood the thing, and had understanding of the vision" — completing the chain of understanding that Gabriel began in Daniel 8:16. The vision of chapters 10–12 tracks empires and kings from Persia through Greece, through the Seleucid-Ptolemaic conflicts, and then into territory the historicist reading identifies as Rome.

Daniel 11:16 describes a power that "shall do according to his own will" (kir'tsono) — a phrase that marks world-empire-level dominance throughout Daniel (see also 8:4 for Medo-Persia; 11:3 for Alexander). The same phrase appears again in Daniel 11:36 for the "willful king," creating a vocabulary chain that marks the transition from one dominant power to another.

Daniel 11:22 refers to "the prince of the covenant" who is broken. This fits within a five-title chain across Daniel pointing to one figure: "Messiah the Prince" (9:25), "the prince of the host" (8:11), "the Prince of princes" (8:25), "the prince of the covenant" (11:22), and "Michael, the great prince" (12:1).

The willful king of Daniel 11:36 is connected to Paul's description in 2 Thessalonians:

"Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition; Who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God, or that is worshipped; so that he as God sitteth in the temple of God, shewing himself that he is God." — 2 Thessalonians 2:3–4

Paul's language matches Daniel 11:36 in structure and vocabulary. Crucially, Paul adds: "the mystery of iniquity doth already work" (2 Thessalonians 2:7) — writing around AD 51. This rules out a purely future antichrist, and it rules out a figure exhausted in the second century BC.

Daniel 12 closes with the eschatological climax:

"And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book. And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt." — Daniel 12:1–2

The title "THE great prince" uses a definite article marking uniqueness — not one among many princes but the specific great prince. The resurrection described here is literal, dual-outcome, and bodily. Daniel himself is promised a place in it: "thou shalt rest, and stand in thy lot at the end of the days" (Daniel 12:13).

docs.title: The New Testament's Use of Daniel
docs.text:
Three New Testament authors draw on Daniel as live prophecy that had not been exhausted.

Jesus, speaking around AD 30, treats the abomination of desolation as still future:

"When ye therefore shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, stand in the holy place, (whoso readeth, let him understand:)" — Matthew 24:15

Mark's account adds a grammatical detail: the word "abomination" is grammatically neuter in Greek, but Mark uses a masculine participle to modify it — a construction indicating the abomination is a person or power, not merely an object.

Paul places Daniel's anti-God figure already at work in his own generation (around AD 51). John structures the entire book of Revelation on Daniel's imagery. Revelation 1:1 opens with a verbatim quotation from Daniel 2:28 in Greek, framing Revelation with Daniel's scope from the very first verse. Revelation 1:13–14 merges the Ancient of Days from Daniel 7 with the Son of Man from Daniel 10 into a single Christological portrait. The four beasts of Daniel 7 are absorbed into Revelation 13's composite beast in reverse order, demonstrating literary dependence.

"And there was given unto him a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies; and power was given unto him to continue forty and two months." — Revelation 13:5–6

The "was given" language in Revelation 13 (edothe, divine passive) indicates that the beast's authority is permitted, not inherent. Its period of dominance is bounded.

The heavenly sanctuary is established in the New Testament as well:

"A minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man." — Hebrews 8:2

Hebrews 8–9 describes Christ as ministering in the heavenly original of which Moses' tabernacle was a copy. This provides the framework for understanding Daniel 8:14's sanctuary vindication as referring to that heavenly reality.

The judgment of Daniel 7 and the judgment hour of Revelation 14 are connected by vocabulary across Greek translation layers:

"Saying with a loud voice, Fear God, and give glory to him; for the hour of his judgment is come: and worship him that made heaven, and earth, and the sea, and the fountains of waters." — Revelation 14:7

The word "judgment" here is krisis — the same word used in the Greek translation of Daniel 7:10. The creation language in Revelation 14:7 echoes the Fourth Commandment in Exodus 20:11 verbatim.

docs.title: What the Bible Does NOT Say
docs.text:
No reading of the evidence should overstate what the text actually contains. The following are not explicitly stated or necessarily implied by Scripture:

  • The text does not name the fourth kingdom. The inference to Rome is strong — one step from three named predecessors, confirmed by New Testament canonical evidence — but it remains an inference.
  • The text does not name the three displaced horns. The traditional identification of three Germanic tribes in the fifth and sixth centuries is a historical argument, not a biblical statement.
  • The day-year principle is not stated as a universal rule applicable to every time period in Scripture. The two direct divine declarations and Daniel's internal signals support applying it to Daniel's apocalyptic time periods, but the application is still one inferential step beyond those declarations.
  • The text does not explicitly identify the little horn of Daniel 7 as the papacy. Nine specifications narrow the identification considerably, but the match to a specific historical institution is an inference from the specifications.
  • The specific starting year of 457 BC for the seventy weeks involves choices among alternatives — calendar reckonings and the reading of Artaxerxes' decree — and is not simply read from the surface of the text.
  • The year 1844 as the terminus of the 2,300-day prophecy depends on the 457 BC starting point, the "cut off from" reading of chathak, and the day-year principle — a chain of three inferences.
  • The text does not name the Sabbath as the specific "law" targeted in Daniel 7:25. The convergence of dat (singular emphatic), zimnin (appointed times), Revelation 14:7's echo of the Fourth Commandment, and Revelation 14:12's description of the faithful as commandment-keepers is substantial, but the Sabbath is not named.
  • The identity of the king of the North and king of the South in Daniel 11:40 and following is genuinely contested among historicist interpreters. Three sub-positions exist and none has been resolved by the text.
  • The starting point of 508 AD for the 1,290 and 1,335-day periods is the weakest chronological claim in the historicist framework. The text does not indicate where these periods begin.
  • The earth as the location of the second beast in Revelation 13:11 being identified with the United States requires a chain of geographic and historical inferences not present in the text itself.

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
The historicist case for Daniel is built from the base of the text outward, not from external history backward. Three kingdoms are named inside Daniel's own text. A fourth follows in a chain the text defines as having no gaps. The horn of Daniel 8 must surpass both named empires — the text sets this up as a mathematical constraint through its own vocabulary. Daniel 8 and 9 are linked by identical grammatical constructions at the beginning and end of Gabriel's commission. The forensic verb of Daniel 8:14 is unique in the entire Old Testament, and it means judicial vindication rather than physical cleansing. The day-year principle rests on two direct divine declarations and is corroborated by multiple signals within Daniel itself. The New Testament treats Daniel's prophecies as active and continuing — Jesus in AD 30, Paul around AD 51, John in Revelation.

The weaknesses in this reading are real and should be held honestly. Where the text names things, the HIST reading stands on firm ground. Where the reading requires matching textual specifications to specific historical institutions — the papacy, the three displaced horns, the 508 AD starting point, the events of Daniel 11:40 and following — the claims are inferences of varying strength, and the study has rated them accordingly. The outer edges of the framework are more uncertain than its core.

The core itself — the four-kingdom sequence, the gadal/yether constraint, the forensic nitsdaq, the biyn chain unity of Daniel 8–9, the Day of Atonement parallels in the judgment scene, the day-year principle, the nine-element reproduction of Daniel 7 in Revelation 4–5, the verbatim quotation of Daniel 2 and 7 in Revelation 1 and 13 — stands on textual evidence that any concordance and lexicon can verify. Sixteen vocabulary chains bind Daniel's four vision cycles into a single prophetic narrative. The same concerns — sovereignty, worship, the sanctuary, times and laws, judgment, and final vindication — run from Daniel 2 through Daniel 12 and forward into Revelation, held together by the same Hebrew and Aramaic roots.

That coherence is itself evidence. The visions present not isolated predictions but a single, sustained prophetic framework, and the New Testament authors treated it as one.

Based on the full technical study completed 2026-03-28

docs.text: The study was checked against the HIST position database (504 arguments across 10 chapter tags and 16 categories) using 12 targeted searches covering all major argument clusters. The following assessment applies.

docs.title: Arguments PRESENT and Adequately Covered
docs.text:
The study accurately and thoroughly represents the following major HIST argument categories from the DB:

The u-vatrakh gap-free succession markers, the d'qaq/parzel vocabulary chain binding Dan 2 and 7, and the ka-chadah simultaneous destruction requirement are all present and correctly stated. L1-MISS-1: The mehem constructio ad sensum argument (Dan 8:9) - Section affected: 03-analysis.md Section 1 (Dan 8:4,8,9); CONCLUSION.md Section IV (Dan 8) - Nature: The DB contains a significant grammar argument about the masculine suffix mehem in Dan 8:9. This argument is relevant to the steelman because it responds to the PRET claim that the horn must arise from one of the four Greek successor kingdoms. The study mentions mehem only tangentially as a keyword in 03-analysis but does not present the actual grammatical argument. - What needs to change: Add a brief treatment of the mehem grammar in the Dan 8 section of CONCLUSION.md (Section IV), noting the masculine/feminine suffix contrast with Dan 7:8, the GKC documentation of the phenomenon, and its significance for the directional (rather than genealogical) reading.

docs.title: L2-ISSUE-1: I-A(2) chain depth for the 2300-year terminus (I7)
docs.text:
• Section: CONCLUSION.md Inferences Table, I7
  • Nature: The study classifies "2300 years from 457 BC -> 1844 AD" as I-A(2) MED. However, this inference depends on THREE prior inferences: (a) I5: chathak = "cut off" from 2300 (I-A(1)); (b) I6: 457 BC starting point (I-A(2)); (c) I3: day-year principle (I-A(1)). The study itself acknowledges this: "Three prior inferences combine; each is independently classified I-A(1) HIGH but the composite carries accumulated uncertainty." If I6 is itself I-A(2), and the 1844 calculation depends on I6 + I5 + I3, the composite should be I-A(3), not I-A(2). Chain depth notation counts the number of inference steps from E/N, not the number of distinct inferences. Here: E/N -> day-year (1 step) -> chathak cut-off (1 step) -> 457 BC start (2 steps from E/N) -> 1844 terminus. The 457 BC start is itself two steps from E/N (requiring decree selection + calendar reckoning), making 1844 at least three steps removed.
  • Classification: CHAIN DEPTH ERROR
  • What needs to change: Reclassify I7 from I-A(2) MED to I-A(3) LOW-MED and update the chain depth notation to reflect that the 1844 terminus depends on at least three prior inference steps from E/N evidence.

docs.title: L2-ISSUE-2: Dan 7 specification #14 (Judgment convenes while horn active) classified I-A(1) HIGH
docs.text:
• Section: CONCLUSION.md, Daniel 7 Specification-Match Matrix, row #14
  • Nature: The study classifies "Judgment convenes while horn active = Pre-advent investigative judgment" as I-A(1) HIGH. The text does state that the judgment convenes (Dan 7:9-10,26) and that the horn is active until the judgment removes its dominion. However, the HIST identification of this as a specifically "pre-advent investigative judgment" beginning in 1844 involves multiple inference steps: (a) the judgment scene is in heaven (N-tier from directional prepositions), (b) the judgment is pre-advent (N-tier from the sequence: judgment THEN kingdom given), but (c) the identification as beginning specifically in 1844 and involving individual case review is I-A(2) or higher, depending on the 2300/sanctuary vindication calculation. The classification should distinguish between the textual observation (judgment precedes kingdom = N-tier) and the full HIST doctrinal identification (investigative judgment beginning 1844 = I-A(2) at best). As written, the I-A(1) HIGH classification conflates these two levels.
  • Classification: MISCLASSIFIED
  • What needs to change: Split this specification into two components: (a) "Judgment convenes before kingdom given" = N-tier (the text states the sequence); (b) "Judgment = pre-advent investigative judgment beginning 1844" = I-A(2) MED (depends on the 2300 calculation and sanctuary theology). Alternatively, clarify that the I-A(1) HIGH classification applies to the textual observation that judgment precedes the Second Coming, not to the full 1844 investigative judgment identification.

docs.title: L2-ISSUE-3: Six DOA parallels classified I-A(1) HIGH without distinguishing direct from typological
docs.text:
• Section: CONCLUSION.md Section III (Daniel 7), paragraph on DOA parallels
  • Nature: The study presents six Day of Atonement parallels in the Dan 7 judgment scene and classifies them collectively as I-A(1) HIGH. However, the study itself acknowledges an important distinction: "The first three have direct Levitical vocabulary correspondences; the latter three operate through typological structure." The first three (white garments, fire/coals, cloud/presence) have verifiable vocabulary links to Leviticus 16. The latter three (books = record examination, Son of Man entering = high priest entering MHP, exclusion from sanctuary) are typological constructions that depend on interpreting the heavenly scene as a Day of Atonement antitype -- which is itself an inference. Classifying all six as I-A(1) HIGH without noting this distinction overstates the uniformity of the evidence. The first three are arguably I-A(1); the latter three are I-A(2) because they depend on the prior inference that the Dan 7 judgment IS a DOA antitype.
  • Classification: MISCLASSIFIED (partial)
  • What needs to change: Either (a) split the six DOA parallels into two tiers: the first three at I-A(1) HIGH (direct vocabulary correspondence) and the latter three at I-A(2) MED (typological inference depending on the DOA identification), or (b) add a qualifying note that the collective I-A(1) HIGH classification applies to the convergence pattern, while acknowledging that the individual typological parallels carry different evidentiary weight.

docs.text:
This is a thorough, well-structured steelman that accurately represents the HIST position at full strength across all of Daniel. The study faithfully reproduces the DB's core arguments -- four-kingdom succession, gadal/yether constraint, nitsdaq forensic vindication, biyn chain inclusio, day-year principle, vocabulary chains, NT continuity, and Daniel-Revelation connections -- with correct citations, Strong's numbers, and linguistic detail.

docs.title: Matthew 24:15 -- bdelygma eremoseos
docs.text:
Greek: Ὅταν οὖν ἴδητε τὸ βδέλυγμα τῆς ἐρημώσεως τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Δανιὴλ τοῦ προφήτου ἑστὸς ἐν τόπῳ ἁγίῳ, ὁ ἀναγινώσκων νοείτω,

Key parsing:
- βδέλυγμα (bdelygma) G946 = [N-ASN] Accusative Singular Neuter "abomination"
- ἐρημώσεως (eremoseos) G2050 = [N-GSF] Genitive Singular Feminine "of desolation"
- τὸ ῥηθὲν (to rhethen) = [T-ASN + V-APP-ASN] "the thing spoken" -- Aorist Passive Participle
- διὰ Δανιὴλ τοῦ προ��ήτου = "through Daniel the prophet" -- Jesus explicitly attributes to Daniel
- ἑστὸς (hestos) = [V-2RAP-ASN] Perfect Active Participle Accusative Singular NEUTER
- ἐν τόπῳ ἁγίῳ = "in a holy place"
- ὁ ἀναγινώσκων νοείτω = "the one reading, let him understand" -- Present Active Imperative
NOTE: In Matthew, hestos is NEUTER (matching bdelygma). Jesus treats Daniel as prophecy still future ("when you shall SEE"). The parenthetical "whoso readeth, let him understand" signals the reader should study Daniel to understand.

docs.title: Mark 13:14 -- hestekota (masculine participle for neuter noun)
docs.text:
Greek: Ὅταν δὲ ἴδητε τὸ βδέλυγμα τῆς ἐρημώσεως ἑστηκότα ὅπου οὐ δεῖ, ὁ ἀναγινώσκων νοείτω,

Key parsing:
- βδέλυγμα (bdelygma) G946 = [N-ASN] Accusative Singular NEUTER "abomination"
- ἑστηκότα (hestekota) = [V-RAP-ASM] Perfect Active Participle Accusative Singular MASCULINE
- ὅπου οὐ δεῖ = "where it ought not" -- standing where it should not be
NOTE: The critical grammatical anomaly -- bdelygma is NEUTER but hestekota is MASCULINE. This constructio ad sensum (agreement by sense rather than grammar) indicates the "abomination" is a PERSON (hence masculine), not merely a thing. Mark deliberately uses the masculine form to signal a personal power behind the abomination. This supports the HIST reading of the horn as a personal/institutional entity.

docs.title: 2 Thessalonians 2:3 -- ho anthropos tes anomias, ho huios tes apoleias
docs.text:
Greek: μή τις ὑμᾶς ἐξαπατήσῃ κατὰ μηδένα τρόπον· ὅτι ἐὰν μὴ ἔλθῃ ἡ ἀποστασία πρῶτον καὶ ἀποκαλυφθῇ ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῆς ἀνομίας, ὁ υἱὸς τῆς ἀπωλείας,

Key parsing:
- ἀποστασία (apostasia) G646 = [N-NSF] "the falling away/apostasy" -- with definite article = THE apostasy
- πρῶτον (proton) = "first" -- apostasy must come BEFORE the Day of Christ
- ἀποκαλυφθῇ (apokalyphthe) = [V-APS-3S] Aorist Passive Subjunctive "be revealed" -- passive = God reveals
- ἄνθρωπος τῆς ἀνομίας = "the man of lawlessness" -- genitive of quality/characteristic
- ἀνομίας (anomias) G458 = [N-GSF] "of lawlessness" -- anomia = violation of law
- υἱὸς τῆς ἀπωλείας = "the son of perdition" -- same title as Judas (John 17:12)
- ἀπωλείας (apoleias) G684 = [N-GSF] "of destruction/perdition"
NOTE: "man of lawlessness" echoes Dan 7:25 "think to change times and LAW" -- the connection between anomia and dat/torah. The title "son of perdition" links to John 17:12 (Judas) and Rev 17:8,11 (the beast) -- three authors, one title for the betrayer-from-within.

docs.title: 2 Thessalonians 2:4 -- self-exaltation, sitting in temple
docs.text:
Greek: ὁ ἀντικείμενος καὶ ὑπεραιρόμενος ἐπὶ πάντα λεγόμενον Θεὸν ἢ σέβασμα, ὥστε αὐτὸν εἰς τὸν ναὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ καθίσαι, ἀποδεικνύντα ἑαυτὸν ὅτι ἔστιν Θεός.

Key parsing:
- ἀντικείμενος (antikemenos) G480 = [V-PNP-NSM] "the one opposing" -- Present Middle/Passive Participle
- ὑπεραιρόμενος (hyperairomenos) G5229 = [V-PPP-NSM] "the one exalting himself above" -- Present Passive Ptcp
- ἐπὶ πάντα λεγόμενον Θεὸν = "above every so-called god" -- above ALL
- σέβασμα (sebasma) G4574 = "object of worship"
- ναὸν (naon) G3485 = "temple/inner shrine" -- NOT hieron; naos = inner sacred space
- καθίσαι (kathisai) = [V-AAN] Aorist Active Infinitive "to sit" -- takes his seat
- ἀποδεικνύντα (apodeiknynta) G584 = [V-PAP-ASM] "displaying/demonstrating"
- ἑαυτὸν ὅτι ἔστιν Θεός = "himself that he is God"
NOTE: Seven structural parallels with Dan 7: 1. Speaking against the Most High (Dan 7:25) = exalts above every god (2 Thess 2:4) 2. Wearing out saints (Dan 7:25) = opposes (2 Thess 2:4) 3. Changing times and law (Dan 7:25) = man of lawlessness (2 Thess 2:3) 4. Revealed/arises (Dan 7:8) = revealed (2 Thess 2:3,8) 5. Until judgment (Dan 7:26) = consumed by brightness of His coming (2 Thess 2:8) 6. From within God's people (implied) = sits in temple of God (2 Thess 2:4) 7. Religious authority (Dan 7:25 dat) = shows himself as God (2 Thess 2:4)

docs.title: 2 Thessalonians 2:7 -- mystery of iniquity ALREADY working
docs.text:
Greek: τὸ γὰρ μυστήριον ἤδη ἐνεργεῖται τῆς ἀνομίας· μόνον ὁ κατέχων ἄρτι ἕως ἐκ μέσου γένηται.

Key parsing:
- μυστήριον (mysterion) G3466 = [N-NSN] "mystery"
- ἤδη (ede) G2235 = [ADV] "already" -- present tense, c. AD 51
- ἐνεργεῖται (energeitai) G1754 = [V-PMI-3S] Present Middle Indicative "is working"
- τῆς ἀνομίας (tes anomias) = "of lawlessness"
- κατέχων (katechon) G2722 = [V-PAP-NSM] Present Active Participle "the one restraining"
- ἄρτι (arti) G737 = [ADV] "now/at this moment"
- ἕως ἐκ μέσου γένηται = "until he be taken out of the way"
NOTE: "ALREADY working" (ede energeitai) in AD 51 rules out: - A purely future individual (FUT) -- it was already active - A purely past figure ending at AD 70 (PRET) -- Paul says it continues until Christ's coming - Only a PROCESS power developing over centuries fits: already active in Paul's day, growing, to be fully revealed, finally destroyed at the Second Coming.

docs.title: Revelation 13:5 -- stoma laloun megala (mouth speaking great things)
docs.text:
Greek: καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ στόμα λαλοῦν μεγάλα καὶ βλασφημίας, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ἐξουσία ποιῆ��αι μῆνας τεσσεράκοντα δύο.

Key parsing:
- ἐδόθη (edothe) G1325 = [V-API-3S] Aorist Passive Indicative "was given" -- divine passive
- στόμα (stoma) G4750 = [N-NSN] "mouth"
- λαλοῦν (laloun) G2980 = [V-PAP-NSN] Present Active Participle "speaking"
- μεγάλα (megala) G3173 = [A-APN] "great things"
- βλασφημίας (blasphemias) G988 = [N-APF] "blasphemies"
- ἐξουσία (exousia) G1849 = [N-NSF] "authority/power"
- μῆνας τεσσεράκοντα δύο = "forty-two months"
NOTE: "stoma laloun megala" is verbatim from Dan 7:8,20 LXX -- "a mouth speaking great things." This is a direct literary quotation. The 42 months (= 1260 days = time/times/half time) connects to Dan 7:25 and Dan 12:7. Rev 13:5-7 reproduces Dan 7:25 point by point: - mouth speaking great things = Dan 7:8 (stoma laloun megala) - blasphemy against God and His tabernacle = Dan 7:25 "words against the Most High" - war with saints and overcome them = Dan 7:21 "made war with saints and prevailed" - 42 months = time/times/half time of Dan 7:25

docs.title: Revelation 13:6 -- three-to-three blasphemy correspondence
docs.text:
Greek: καὶ ἤνοιξεν τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ εἰς βλασφημίας πρὸς τὸν Θεόν, βλασφημῆσαι τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν σκηνὴν αὐτοῦ, τοὺς ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ σκηνοῦντας.

Key parsing:
- βλασφημῆσαι (blasphemesai) G987 = [V-AAN] Aorist Active Infinitive "to blaspheme"
- Three objects of blasphemy:
  1. τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ = "His name" (God's identity/authority)
  2. τὴν σκηνὴν αὐτοῦ = "His tabernacle" (God's dwelling/sanctuary)
  3. τοὺς ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ σκηνοῦντας = "those who dwell in heaven" (God's people/angels)
- σκηνὴν (skenen) G4633 = "tent/tabernacle" -- heavenly sanctuary
- σκηνοῦντας (skenountas) G4637 = [V-PAP-APM] "those tabernacling/dwelling"
NOTE: Three-to-three correspondence with Dan 7:25: Dan 7:25a: "speak against the Most High" = Rev 13:6a "blaspheme His name" Dan 7:25b: "wear out the saints" = Rev 13:6c "blaspheme those dwelling in heaven" Dan 7:25c: "think to change times and law" = Rev 13:6b "blaspheme His tabernacle" (where the law is kept)

docs.title: Revelation 14:7 -- hora tes kriseos (hour of judgment) + creation language
docs.text:
Greek: λέγων ἐν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ· Φοβήθητε τὸν Θεὸν καὶ δότε αὐτῷ δόξαν, ὅτι ἦλθεν ἡ ὥρα τῆς κρίσεως αὐτοῦ, καὶ προσκυνήσατε τῷ ποιήσαντι τὸν οὐρα��ὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ θάλασσαν καὶ πηγὰς ὑδάτων.

Key parsing:
- ἦλθεν (elthen) G2064 = [V-2AAI-3S] Aorist Active Indicative "came/has come"
- ὥρα (hora) G5610 = [N-NSF] "hour"
- κρίσε��ς (kriseos) G2920 = [N-GSF] "of judgment"
- προσκυνήσατε (proskynesate) G4352 = [V-AAM-2P] Aorist Active Imperative "worship!"
- τῷ ποιήσαντι (to poiesanti) G4160 = [V-AAP-DSM] Aorist Active Participle Dative "the One who made"
- τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ θάλασσαν καὶ πηγὰς ὑδάτων = "heaven and earth and sea and fountains of waters"
NOTE: This verse UNIQUELY converges two themes: 1. JUDGMENT: "the hour of His krisis" -- krisis traces via LXX to Dan 7:10 (dina = krisis). This bridges from Dan 7 judgment scene to Dan 8:14 sanctuary vindication. 2. CREATION/SABBATH: "worship Him who made heaven and earth and the sea" -- verbatim echo of Exo 20:11 (Fourth Commandment). This connects judgment with Sabbath/creation. The convergence: Rev 14:7 calls for worship of the Creator (Exo 20 language) because the hour of judgment (Dan 7/8 language) has come. This is the HIST identification verse: the judgment of Dan 8:14 triggers a Sabbath-creation call to worship.

docs.title: Revelation 1:1 -- esemainen (signified) + ha dei genesthai
docs.text:
Greek: Ἀποκάλυψις Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἣν ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ ὁ Θεός, δεῖξαι τοῖς δούλοις αὐτοῦ ἃ δεῖ γενέσθαι ἐν τάχει, καὶ ἐσήμανεν ἀποστείλας διὰ τοῦ ἀγγέλου αὐτοῦ, τῷ δούλῳ αὐτοῦ Ἰωάνῃ,

Key parsing:
- Ἀποκάλυψις (apokalypsis) G602 = [N-NSF] "revelation/unveiling"
- ἃ δεῖ γενέσθαι (ha dei genesthai) = "things which must come to pass" -- δεῖ [V-PAI-3S] "it is necessary" + γενέσθαι [V-2ADN] Aor Mid Inf "to happen"
- ἐν τάχει (en tachei) = "in/with speed" -- NOT "immediately" but "when they begin, they come quickly"
- ἐσήμανεν (esemainen) G4591 = [V-AAI-3S] Aorist Active Indicative "He signified/communicated through signs"
- ἀποστείλας (aposteilas) G649 = [V-AAP-NSM] Aorist Active Participle "having sent"
NOTE: (1) ha dei genesthai is VERBATIM from Dan 2:28-29,45 LXX ("the things that must come to pass"). In Daniel 2, this content spans Nebuchadnezzar's day to the end of time. John deliberately frames Revelation with Daniel's trans-historical scope. (2) esemainen = "communicated through signs/symbols" -- every NT occurrence of semaino involves indirect sign-mediated communication (John 12:33; 18:32; 21:19; Acts 11:28; 25:27). This establishes from the opening verse that Revelation's beasts, horns, time periods, etc. are symbolic codes. (3) en tachei cannot restrict Revelation to first-century events given the Danielic framing.

docs.title: Revelation 12:5 -- eteken, herpasthe (aorist past-tense argument)
docs.text:
Greek: καὶ ἔτεκεν υἱόν, ἄρσεν, ὃς μέλλει ποιμαίνειν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη ἐν ῥάβδῳ σιδηρᾷ· καὶ ἡρπάσθη τὸ τέκνον αὐτῆς πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν καὶ πρὸς τὸν θρόνον αὐτοῦ.

Key parsing:
- ἔτεκεν (eteken) G5088 = [V-2AAI-3S] Aorist Active Indicative "she brought forth" -- PAST completed
- ἄρσεν (arsen) G730 = [A-ASN] "male" -- NEUTER agreeing with teknon
- ὃς (hos) G3739 = [R-NSM] Relative Pronoun MASCULINE -- agreement by sense with "son/child"
- μέλλει ποιμαίνειν (mellei poimainein) = "is about to rule/shepherd" -- future from the vision's perspective
- ῥάβδῳ σιδηρᾷ (rhabdo sidera) = "with a rod of iron" -- echoes Ps 2:9 and Rev 2:27; 19:15
- ἡρπάσθη (herpasthe) G726 = [V-API-3S] Aorist Passive Indicative "was caught up/snatched away" -- PAST completed
- τέκνον (teknon) G5043 = [N-NSN] "child" -- neuter
NOTE: TWO aorist indicative verbs describe COMPLETED PAST events: Christ's birth (eteken) and ascension (herpasthe). If Rev 4-22 were entirely future (as FUT requires), these past events should not appear within the prophetic narrative. The rod-of-iron allusion to Ps 2:9 identifies the child as Christ. The passive herpasthe ("was snatched away") = divine passive, indicating God's protective intervention at the ascension.

docs.title: Revelation 13:11 -- arnion (lamb-like beast)
docs.text:
Greek: Καὶ εἶδον ἄλλο θηρίον ἀναβαῖνον ἐκ τῆς γῆς, καὶ εἶχεν κέρατα δύο ὅμοια ἀρνίῳ, καὶ ἐλάλει ὡς δράκων.

Key parsing:
- ἄλλο (allo) G243 = [A-ASN] "another (of the same kind)" -- another beast
- ἀναβαῖνον (anabainon) G305 = [V-PAP-ASN] Present Active Participle "coming up/rising"
- ἐκ τῆς γῆς (ek tes ges) = "out of the earth" -- NOT from the sea (Rev 13:1; 17:15 sea = peoples)
- κέρατα δύο (kerata duo) = "two horns"
- ὅμοια ἀρνίῳ (homoia arnio) G3664 + G721 = "like a lamb" -- arnion = Christological diminutive
- ἐλάλει (elalei) G2980 = [V-IAI-3S] Imperfect Active Indicative "was speaking" -- ongoing speech
- ὡς δράκων (hos drakon) = "as a dragon" -- dragon-like speech
NOTE: arnion (G721) appears 30x in Revelation -- 29x for Christ, 1x here for the beast's imitation. The lamb-like horns WITHOUT crowns (contrast 12:3; 13:1 which have crowns) suggest principles rather than monarchies. Rising from "earth" (ge) vs "sea" = sparsely populated territory. The imperfect elalei ("was speaking") = ongoing/developing speech -- initially lamb-like, progressively dragon-like.

docs.title: Revelation 11:19 -- naos, kibotos, theophany
docs.text:
Greek: καὶ ἠνοίγη ὁ ναὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ ὁ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, καὶ ὤφθη ἡ κιβωτὸς τῆς διαθήκης αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ ναῷ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐγένοντο ἀστραπαὶ καὶ φωναὶ καὶ βρονταὶ καὶ σεισμὸς καὶ χάλαζα μεγάλη.

Key parsing:
- ἠνοίγη (enoige) G455 = [V-2API-3S] Aorist Passive Indicative "was opened"
- ναὸς (naos) G3485 = [N-NSM] "temple/inner shrine" -- NOT hieron (temple precincts)
- ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ (en to ourano) = "in heaven" -- the HEAVENLY temple
- ὤφθη (ophthe) G3708 = [V-API-3S] Aorist Passive Indicative "was seen/appeared"
- κιβωτὸς (kibotos) G2787 = [N-NSF] "ark/chest" -- THE ark of the covenant
- διαθήκης (diathekes) G1242 = [N-GSF] "of the covenant/testament"
- ἀστραπαί, φωναί, βρονταί, σεισμός, χάλαζα = lightnings, voices, thunders, earthquake, hail
NOTE: The ark of the covenant -- the repository of the Ten Commandments -- is seen in the heavenly temple. Revelation uses naos (inner shrine) 16x and NEVER hieron. This is the Most Holy Place of the heavenly sanctuary. The theophany formula (lightnings + voices + thunders + earthquake + hail) at Rev 11:19 is the third escalation stage (after 4:5 and 8:5), marking the transition to the MHP phase.

docs.title: Revelation 2:25 -- achri hou an hexo (till I come)
docs.text:
Greek: πλὴν ὃ ἔχετε κρατήσατε ἄχρι οὗ ἂν ἥξω.

Key parsing:
- πλὴν (plen) G4133 = [ADV] "nevertheless/only"
- κρατήσατε (kratesate) G2902 = [V-AAM-2P] Aorist Active Imperative "hold fast!"
- ἄχρι (achri) G891 = [ADV] "until"
- οὗ (hou) G3739 = [R-GSM] Relative Pronoun "which" (= the time when)
- ἂν (an) G302 = [PRT] contingency particle
- ἥξω (hexo) G2240 = [V-AAS-1S] Aorist Active Subjunctive "I come"
NOTE: achri hou an hexo = "until whenever I come" -- an indefinite temporal clause extending to Christ's return. This appears at the FOURTH of seven churches (Thyatira). If the seven churches represent sequential historical eras, this clause extends the sequence to the Second Coming. Rev 3:3 adds "I will come as a thief" at the fifth church (Sardis). These single verses refute confining all seven churches to the first century alone.

docs.title: Luke 23:56 -- kata ten entolen (according to THE commandment)
docs.text:
Greek: Καὶ τὸ μὲν σάββατον ἡσύχασαν κατὰ τὴν ἐντολήν,

Key parsing:
- σάββατον (sabbaton) G4521 = [N-ASN] "sabbath"
- ἡσύχασαν (hesychasan) G2270 = [V-AAI-3P] Aorist Active Indicative "they rested"
- κατὰ (kata) G2596 = [PREP] "according to"
- τὴν (ten) G3588 = [T-ASF] THE -- definite article = specific, known commandment
- ἐντολήν (entolen) G1785 = [N-ASF] "commandment"
NOTE: kata ten entolen = "according to THE commandment" -- the definite article specifies a particular, known commandment (= the Fourth Commandment, Exo 20:8-11). This is written AFTER the crucifixion, indicating the Sabbath commandment remained in force. Luke, a Gentile author writing to Gentiles (Theophilus), treats "the commandment" as self-evidently referring to the Sabbath.

docs.title: 2 Thessalonians 2:8 -- ho anomos (the lawless one)
docs.text:
Greek: καὶ τότε ἀποκαλυφθήσεται ὁ ἄνομος, ὃν ὁ Κύριος Ἰησοῦς ἀνελεῖ τῷ πνεύματι τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ καὶ καταργήσει τῇ ἐπιφανείᾳ τῆς παρουσίας αὐτοῦ,

Key parsing:
- ἀποκαλυφθήσεται (apokalyphthesetai) G601 = [V-FPI-3S] Future Passive Indicative "will be revealed"
- ὁ ἄνομος (ho anomos) G459 = [T-NSM + A-NSM] "THE lawless one" -- substantival adjective with article
- ἀνελεῖ (anelei) G337 = [V-2FAI-3S] Future Active Indicative "will destroy/consume"
- τῷ πνεύματι τοῦ στόματος (to pneumati tou stomatos) = "by the breath/spirit of His mouth"
- καταργήσει (katargesei) G2673 = [V-FAI-3S] Future Active Indicative "will render inoperative/abolish"
- τῇ ἐπιφανείᾳ (te epiphaneia) G2015 = [N-DSF] "by the brightness/appearing"
- τῆς παρουσίας (tes parousias) G3952 = [N-GSF] "of the coming/presence"
NOTE: ho anomos = "the lawless one" (a-nomos = without-law/against-law). Paul uses TWO verbs for the destruction: anelei ("consume/slay" by the breath of His mouth) and katargesei ("render inoperative/abolish" by the brightness of His coming). The double destruction verb suggests a two-stage process: progressive weakening + final elimination at the parousia. This parallels Dan 7:26 "they shall take away his dominion, to consume and to destroy it unto the end."

docs.title: Revelation 5:1 -- katasphragismenon (sealed with seven seals)
docs.text:
Greek: βιβλίον γεγραμμένον ἔσωθεν καὶ ὄπισθεν, κατεσφραγισμένον σφραγῖσιν ἑπτά.

Key parsing:
- βιβλίον (biblion) G975 = [N-ASN] "scroll/book"
- γεγραμμένον (gegrammenon) G1125 = [V-RPP-ASN] Perfect Passive Participle "having been written"
- ἔσωθεν καὶ ὄπισθεν (esothen kai opisthen) = "inside and on the back" -- completely full
- κατεσφραγισμένον (katesphragismenon) G2696 = [V-RPP-ASN] Perfect Passive Participle "having been sealed up"
- σφραγῖσιν ἑπτά (sphragisin hepta) = "with seven seals"
NOTE: katasphragizo (G2696) is an NT HAPAX -- found only here. The kata- prefix intensifies the sealing: "sealed up completely." This is the third stage in the sealed-to-unsealed arc: (1) Dan 8:26 satham (Qal); (2) Dan 12:4 satham + chatham (double seal); (3) Rev 5:1 katasphragizo (intensified NT hapax). The perfect passive participle indicates a STATE: the scroll IS sealed and REMAINS sealed until the Lamb opens it.

docs.title: Revelation 22:10 -- me sphragises (do not seal)
docs.text:
Greek: Μὴ σφραγίσῃς τοὺς λόγους τῆς προφητείας τοῦ βιβλίου τούτου· ὁ καιρὸς γὰρ ἐγγύς ἐστιν.

Key parsing:
- Μὴ (me) G3361 = [PRT-N] negative particle
- σφραγίσῃς (sphragises) G4972 = [V-AAS-2S] Aorist Active Subjunctive "you should seal"
- τοὺς λόγους (tous logous) = "the words"
- τῆς προφητείας (tes propheteias) = "of the prophecy"
- ὁ καιρὸς ἐγγύς ἐστιν (ho kairos engys estin) = "the time is near"
NOTE: me + aorist subjunctive = prohibitive subjunctive = "do not even BEGIN to seal." This is the fifth and final stage of the sealed-to-unsealed arc: (1) Dan 8:26 shut up; (2) Dan 12:4 double-sealed; (3) Rev 5:1 intensified sealing; (4) Rev 10:2 open (eneogmenon, perfect passive = "having been opened and remaining open"); (5) Rev 22:10 command not to seal. The arc reversal proves Revelation's content is now accessible -- Daniel's sealed prophecies are UNSEALED through Revelation.

docs.title: Revelation 7:3 -- sphragis (seal of God)
docs.text:
Greek: ἄχρι σφραγίσωμεν τοὺς δούλους τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν ἐπὶ τῶν μετώπων αὐτῶν.

Key parsing:
- σφραγίσωμεν (sphragisomen) G4972 = [V-AAS-1P] Aorist Active Subjunctive "we seal"
- δούλους (doulous) G1401 = [N-APM] "servants/slaves"
- μετώπων (metopon) G3359 = [N-GPN] "foreheads" -- FOREHEAD only (no hand)
NOTE: God's seal is placed on the FOREHEAD only -- location of thought/allegiance. Compare Rev 13:16 where the mark (charagma) is placed on forehead OR hand. This contrast (seal = forehead only; mark = forehead or hand) suggests the seal involves conscious conviction while the mark includes either conviction or coerced compliance.

docs.title: Revelation 13:16 -- charagma (mark)
docs.text:
Greek: ἵνα δῶσιν αὐτοῖς χάραγμα ἐπὶ τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῶν τῆς δεξιᾶς ἢ ἐπὶ τὸ μέτωπον αὐτῶν,

Key parsing:
- χάραγμα (charagma) G5480 = [N-ASN] "mark/stamp/brand" -- from charasso = engrave
- ἐπὶ τῆς χειρὸς (epi tes cheiros) = "upon the hand"
- τῆς δεξιᾶς (tes dexias) = "the right (hand)"
- ἢ (e) G2228 = [PRT] "OR"
- ἐπὶ τὸ μέτωπον (epi to metopon) = "upon the forehead"
NOTE: charagma = an engraved stamp/brand (used of images on coins, imperial seals). The OR between hand and forehead means the mark involves EITHER conscious allegiance (forehead) OR external compliance/action (hand). This contrasts with God's seal which is forehead ONLY -- requiring genuine conviction.

docs.title: Daniel 2:38 -- anteh-hu emphatic pronoun
docs.text:
וּבְכָל־דִּ֣י דָֽיְרִ֣ין בְּֽנֵי־אֲ֠נָשָׁא חֵיוַ֨ת בָּרָ֤א וְעֹוף־שְׁמַיָּא֙ יְהַ֣ב בִּידָ֔ךְ וְהַשְׁלְטָ֖ךְ בְּכָלְּהֹ֑ון אַנְתְּ־ה֔וּא רֵאשָׁ֖ה דִּ֥י דַהֲבָֽא׃

Key parsing:
- אנתה (anteh) = PersPron.2ms "you"
- ה֔וּא (hu') = PersPron.3ms "he"
- Together: anteh-hu = emphatic "YOU (are) HE" = "Thou art this head of gold"
- רֵאשָׁ֖ה (re'shah) = Noun.ms "head"
- דַהֲבָֽא (dahaba') = Noun.ms "gold"
- יְהַ֣ב (yehab) = Verb.peal.Perf.3ms "give" -- God GAVE authority
- הַשְׁלְטָ֖ךְ (hashletakh) = Verb.haf.Perf.3ms+2ms "caused you to rule"
NOTE: anteh-hu is E-tier identification -- the text explicitly names Babylon.

docs.title: Daniel 7:25 -- bela, shanah, sbar, dat, 'iddan
docs.text:
וּמִלִּ֗ין לְצַ֤ד עִלָּאָה֙ יְמַלִּ֔ל וּלְקַדִּישֵׁ֥י עֶלְיֹונִ֖ין יְבַלֵּ֑א וְיִסְבַּ֗ר לְהַשְׁנָיָה֙ זִמְנִ֣ין וְדָ֔ת וְיִתְיַהֲב֣וּן בִּידֵ֔הּ עַד־עִדָּ֥ן וְעִדָּנִ֖ין וּפְלַ֥ג עִדָּֽן׃

Key parsing:
- מִלִּ֗ין (millin) = Noun.fp.Abs "words" -- the horn's distinctive speech
- יְמַלִּ֔ל (yemallil) = Verb.pael.Impf.3ms "speak" -- Pael (intensive) = great/bombastic speech
- יְבַלֵּ֑א (yeballe') = Verb.pael.Impf.3ms "wear out" -- HAPAX, Pael imperfect = sustained attrition
- יִסְבַּ֗ר (yisbar) = Verb.peal.Impf.3ms "intend/think" -- NOT "succeed" but "plan/attempt"
- לְהַשְׁנָיָה֙ (lehashnayyah) = Verb.haf.InfCon "to change" -- Haphel (causative) of shanah
- זִמְנִ֣ין (zimnin) = Noun.mp.Abs "times" -- appointed times/seasons
- דָ֔ת (dat) = Noun.fs.Abs "law" -- absolute form (no possessive) = THE law (God's)
- עִדָּ֥ן (iddan) = Noun.ms.Abs "time" -- year (per BDB and Dan 4 usage)
- עִדָּנִ֖ין (iddanin) = Noun.mp.Abs "times" -- plural
- פְלַ֥ג (pelag) = Noun.ms.Cst "half"
NOTES: - bela Pael imperfect = prolonged wearing action, not sudden destruction - sbar = "intend/think" -- indicates attempted, not necessarily accomplished change - dat in absolute = God's law (cf. Dan 6:5 where dat is used for God's law) - 'iddan + 'iddanin + pelag 'iddan = 1 + 2 + 0.5 = 3.5 years/times

docs.title: Daniel 8:9 -- gadal with yether (exceeding great)
docs.text:
וּמִן־הָאַחַ֣ת מֵהֶ֔ם יָצָ֥א קֶֽרֶן־אַחַ֖ת מִצְּעִירָ֑ה וַתִּגְדַּל־יֶ֛תֶר אֶל־הַנֶּ֥גֶב וְאֶל־הַמִּזְרָ֖ח וְאֶל־הַצֶּֽבִי׃

Key parsing:
- מִצְּעִירָ֑ה (mits'eirah) = Noun.fs.Abs "youth/smallness" -- HAPAX, extreme littleness at origin
- וַתִּגְדַּל (vattigdal) = Verb.Qal.Wayq.3fs "became great" -- QAL stem (intransitive)
- יֶ֛תֶר (yether) = Noun.ms.Abs "remainder/excess" -- adverbial modifier = "exceedingly"
NOTE: Three-stage gadal escalation: 1. Dan 8:4 -- ram gadal (became great) -- no modifier 2. Dan 8:8 -- goat gadal ad me'od (became very great) -- me'od modifier 3. Dan 8:9 -- horn gadal yether (became exceedingly great) -- yether modifier The horn MUST surpass both the named empires (Medo-Persia and Greece).

docs.title: Daniel 8:14 -- nitsdaq (forensic vindication)
docs.text:
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י עַ֚ד עֶ֣רֶב בֹּ֔קֶר אַלְפַּ֖יִם וּשְׁלֹ֣שׁ מֵאֹ֑ות וְנִצְדַּ֖ק קֹֽדֶשׁ׃

Key parsing:
- עֶ֣רֶב (erev) = Noun.ms.Abs "evening"
- בֹּ֔קֶר (boqer) = Noun.ms.Abs "morning"
- אַלְפַּ֖יִם (alpayim) = Noun.d.Abs "two thousand" (dual)
- שְׁלֹ֣שׁ מֵאֹ֑ות (shelosh me'ot) = "three hundred"
- נִצְדַּ֖ק (nitsdaq) = Verb.Niphal.Perf.3ms "be justified/vindicated" -- ONLY Niphal of tsadaq
- קֹֽדֶשׁ (qodesh) = Noun.ms.Abs "holiness/sanctuary"
NOTES: - nitsdaq is the ONLY Niphal form of tsadaq in the entire OT - Niphal of tsadaq = forensic/declarative: "be declared righteous" = vindicated - This is NOT the ritual word taher ("cleanse") -- it is a judicial term - erev-boqer echoes Gen 1:5,8 creation formula -- suggests day units, not evening-morning sacrifices - The sanctuary is declared righteous/vindicated through a forensic process

docs.title: Daniel 8:23 -- az paniym (fierce countenance) construct chain
docs.text:
וּֽבְאַחֲרִית֙ מַלְכוּתָ֔ם כְּהָתֵ֖ם הַפֹּשְׁעִ֑ים יַעֲמֹ֛ד מֶ֥לֶךְ עַז־פָּנִ֖ים וּמֵבִ֥ין חִידֹֽות׃

Key parsing:
- אַחֲרִית֙ (acharith) = Noun.fs.Cst "end" -- "latter time of their kingdom"
- מַלְכוּתָ֔ם (malkutam) = Noun.fs.Abs+3mp "their kingship"
- הָתֵ֖ם (hatem) = Verb.Hiphil.InfCon "when they are complete" -- transgressors come to fullness
- הַפֹּשְׁעִ֑ים (happoshe'im) = Verb.Qal.Ptcp.mp "the rebels/transgressors"
- מֶ֥לֶךְ (melekh) = Noun.ms.Abs "king"
- עַז (az) = Adj.ms.Cst "strong/fierce" (H5794)
- פָּנִ֖ים (paniym) = Noun.mp.Abs "face" (H6440)
- מֵבִ֥ין (mevin) = Verb.Hiphil.Ptcp.ms "understanding" -- from biyn
- חִידֹֽות (chidot) = Noun.fp.Abs "riddles/dark sentences"
NOTE: az-paniym ONLY occurs in Deut 28:50 and Dan 8:23 -- a covenant-curse construct chain. Deut 28:49-50 describes a nation God brings as covenant punishment: "a nation of fierce countenance" (az paniym). Dan 8:23 applies the same phrase. This links the horn to the covenant-curse tradition.

docs.title: Daniel 9:24 -- six infinitives, chathak
docs.text:
שָׁבֻעִ֨ים שִׁבְעִ֜ים נֶחְתַּ֥ךְ עַֽל־עַמְּךָ֣׀ וְעַל־עִ֣יר קָדְשֶׁ֗ךָ לְכַלֵּ֨א הַפֶּ֜שַׁע וּלְהָתֵ֤ם חַטָּאת֙ וּלְכַפֵּ֣ר עָוֹ֔ן וּלְהָבִ֖יא צֶ֣דֶק עֹֽלָמִ֑ים וְלַחְתֹּם֙ חָזֹ֣ון וְנָבִ֔יא וְלִמְשֹׁ֖חַ קֹ֥דֶשׁ קָֽדָשִֽׁים׃

Key parsing:
- שָׁבֻעִ֨ים שִׁבְעִ֜ים (shabu'im shiv'im) = "seventy weeks/sevens"
- נֶחְתַּ֥ךְ (nechtak) = Verb.Niphal.Perf.3ms of חתך (chathak) = "be cut off/determined" -- HAPAX
- Six infinitive constructs with ל (le-):
  1. לְכַלֵּ֨א (lekhalle') = Piel InfCon of כלה = "to finish/restrain" -- the transgression (pesha)
  2. לְהָתֵ֤ם (lehatem) = Hiphil InfCon of תמם = "to seal up/complete" -- sins (chatta'ot)
  3. לְכַפֵּ֣ר (lekhapper) = Piel InfCon of כפר = "to cover/atone" -- iniquity (avon)
  4. לְהָבִ֖יא (lehavi') = Hiphil InfCon of בוא = "to bring in" -- everlasting righteousness (tsedeq olamim)
  5. לַחְתֹּם֙ (lachtom) = Qal InfCon of חתם = "to seal" -- vision and prophecy (chazon ve-navi')
  6. לִמְשֹׁ֖חַ (limeshoach) = Qal InfCon of משׁח = "to anoint" -- most holy (qodesh qodashim)
NOTES: - chathak (H2852) ONLY occurs here -- Daniel's deliberate word choice vs. charats (H2782) - DOA triad: pesha + chatta'ot + avon = same three sin categories as Lev 16:21 (Day of Atonement) - The upgrade pattern: the first three infinitives REMOVE sin; the last three ESTABLISH God's program - kaphar-to-tsedeq: from "covering" sin to "everlasting righteousness" -- an upgrade from Levitical system

docs.title: Daniel 11:36 -- kir'tsono, za'am, necheratsah
docs.text:
וְעָשָׂ֨ה כִרְצֹונֹ֜ו הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וְיִתְרֹומֵ֤ם וְיִתְגַּדֵּל֙ עַל־כָּל־אֵ֔ל וְעַל֙ אֵ֣ל אֵלִ֔ים יְדַבֵּ֖ר נִפְלָאֹ֑ות וְהִצְלִ֨יחַ֙ עַד־כָּ֣לָה זַ֔עַם כִּ֥י נֶחֱרָצָ֖ה נֶעֱשָֽׂתָה׃

Key parsing:
- כִרְצֹונֹ֜ו (kir'tsono) = Prep+Noun.ms+3ms "according to his will/pleasure"
- יִתְרֹומֵ֤ם (yitromem) = Verb.Hithpael.Impf.3ms of רום = "exalt himself"
- יִתְגַּדֵּל֙ (yitgaddel) = Verb.Hithpael.Impf.3ms of גדל = "magnify himself"
- אֵ֣ל אֵלִ֔ים ('el 'elim) = "God of gods"
- נִפְלָאֹ֑ות (nifla'ot) = Verb.Niphal.Ptcp.fp "wonderful/astonishing things"
- זַ֔עַם (za'am) = Noun.ms.Abs "indignation/curse"
- נֶחֱרָצָ֖ה (necheratsah) = Verb.Niphal.Ptcp.fs of חרץ = "that which is decreed/determined"
NOTES: - kir'tsono chain: Dan 8:4 (ram), 11:3 (Alexander), 11:16 (Rome enters), 11:36 (willful king) - The same phrase tracks the succession: each power "does according to its will" - za'am bracket: Dan 8:19 "last end of the indignation" and 11:36 "till the indignation be accomplished" -- same za'am bookends chapters 8 and 11 - necheratsah chain: Dan 9:26,27 and 11:36 -- same root charats ("determined") - Four converging vocabulary lines at 11:36: (1) kir'tsono from 8:4/11:3/11:16; (2) yitgaddel from gadal chain; (3) 'el 'elim echoing Dan 7:25 "against the Most High"; (4) necheratsah from Dan 9:26-27

docs.title: Daniel 12:1 -- ya'amod, Michael, sar ha-gadol
docs.text:
וּבָעֵ֣ת הַהִיא֩ יַעֲמֹ֨ד מִֽיכָאֵ֜ל הַשַּׂ֣ר הַגָּדֹ֗ול הָעֹמֵד֮ עַל־בְּנֵ֣י עַמֶּךָ֒

Key parsing:
- יַעֲמֹ֨ד (ya'amod) = Verb.Qal.Impf.3ms of עמד = "stand/arise"
- מִֽיכָאֵ֜ל (Mikha'el) = PropN.ms "Michael" = "Who is like God?"
- הַשַּׂ֣ר (ha-sar) = Art+Noun.ms "THE prince" -- definite article = specific, unique
- הַגָּדֹ֗ול (ha-gadol) = Art+Adj.ms "THE great" -- superlative
- הָעֹמֵד֮ (ha-'omed) = Art+Verb.Qal.Ptcp.ms "the one standing"
- בְּנֵ֣י עַמֶּךָ֒ (benei 'ammekha) = "children of your people"
- עֵ֣ת צָרָ֔ה ('et tsarah) = "time of distress/trouble"
- יִמָּלֵ֣ט (yimmalet) = Verb.Niphal.Impf.3ms "be delivered/escape"
- כָּת֥וּב בַּסֵּֽפֶר (kathuv bassepher) = "written in the book"
NOTES: - Michael = ha-sar ha-gadol -- the definite articles make this THE prince, THE great one - "stands for" (ya'amod + 'al) = intervenes on behalf of - "written in the book" parallels the judgment books of Dan 7:10 - Michael title progression: "one of the chief princes" (10:13) -> "your prince" (10:21) -> "the great prince" (12:1)

docs.title: Daniel 7:9 -- judgment scene, thrones, Ancient of Days
docs.text:
חָזֵ֣ה הֲוֵ֗ית עַ֣ד דִּ֤י כָרְסָוָן֙ רְמִ֔יו וְעַתִּ֥יק יֹומִ֖ין יְתִ֑ב

Key parsing:
- כָרְסָוָן (korsavan) = Noun.mp.Abs "thrones" (plural!)
- רְמִ֔יו (remiyu) = Verb.peil.Perf.3mp "were cast/placed" (Peil passive of remah = throw)
- עַתִּ֥יק (attiq) = Adj.ms.Cst "ancient/old" -- construct with yomin
- יֹומִ֖ין (yomin) = Noun.mp.Abs "days" -- Ancient of Days
- יְתִ֑ב (yetib) = Verb.peal.Perf.3ms "sat" -- from yetab = sit
- לְבוּשֵׁ֣הּ (levusheh) = Noun.ms.Abs+3ms "his garment"
- כִּתְלַ֣ג חִוָּ֗ר (kitlag chivvar) = "like snow, white" -- white garments
- שְׂעַ֤ר רֵאשֵׁהּ֙ כַּעֲמַ֣ר נְקֵ֔א (se'ar resheh ka'amar neqe) = "hair of his head like pure wool"
- כָּרְסְיֵהּ֙ שְׁבִיבִ֣ין דִּי־נ֔וּר (korseyyeh shevivin di-nur) = "his throne, flames of fire"
- גַּלְגִּלֹּ֖והִי נ֥וּר דָּלִֽק (galgilllohi nur daliq) = "its wheels, burning fire"
NOTE: remiyu (Peil passive 3mp) = "were placed/set up" -- thrones (plural) set up for judgment. The KJV "cast down" is misleading; the Aramaic means thrones were PLACED/ESTABLISHED (not overthrown). White garments + fire + wheels = DOA high-priestly and theophanic elements. Rev 1:14 merges this white-hair description with Daniel 10:6's fire.

docs.title: Daniel 7:10 -- dina yetib, sifrin petichu
docs.text:
נְהַ֣ר דִּי־נ֗וּר ... דִּינָ֥א יְתִ֖ב וְסִפְרִ֥ין פְּתִֽיחוּ

Key parsing:
- נְהַ֣ר (nehar) = Noun.ms.Abs "river" -- river of fire
- נָגֵ֤ד (naged) = Verb.peal.Ptcp.ms "flowing" -- continuous flow
- נָפֵק֙ (napheq) = Verb.peal.Ptcp.ms "going out"
- אֶ֤לֶף אַלְפִין֙ (eleph alphin) = "thousand thousands"
- יְשַׁמְּשׁוּנֵּ֔הּ (yeshammeshunneh) = Verb.pael.Impf.3mp+3ms "served him" -- Pael = intensive service
- רִבֹּ֥ו רִבְבָ֖ן (ribbo ribbevan) = "myriad myriads" (= ten thousand times ten thousand)
- יְקוּמ֑וּן (yequmun) = Verb.peal.Impf.3mp "stood" -- stood before him
- דִּינָ֥א (dina) = Noun.ms "judgment" -- THE judgment
- יְתִ֖ב (yetib) = Verb.peal.Perf.3ms "sat" -- the court SAT (convened)
- סִפְרִ֥ין (sifrin) = Noun.mp.Abs "books"
- פְּתִֽיחוּ (petichu) = Verb.peil.Perf.3mp "were opened"
NOTE: dina yetib = "the court sat/convened" -- forensic judgment scene with formal session. sifrin petichu = "books were opened" -- record-based examination. The identical formula "myriads myriads" (ribbo ribbevan) appears in Rev 5:11, confirming literary dependence.

docs.title: Daniel 7:8 -- aqar (uproot), horn details
docs.text:
וּתְלָ֗ת מִן־קַרְנַיָּא֙ קַדְמָ֣יָתָ֔א אֶתְעֲקַ֖רָה מִן־קֳדָמַ֑הּ

Key parsing:
- קֶ֣רֶן אָחֳרִ֤י זְעֵירָה֙ (qeren ochorey ze'irah) = "another little horn"
- סִלְקָ֣ת (silqat) = Verb.peal.Perf.3fs "went up/arose" -- rose among them
- אֶתְעֲקַ֖רָה (et'aqarah) = Verb.etpe.Perf.3fp of עקר ('aqar) = "were uprooted"
- עַיְנִ֜ין כְּעַיְנֵ֤י אֲנָשָׁא֙ (aynin ke'ayney anasha) = "eyes like eyes of a man"
- פֻ֖ם מְמַלִּ֥ל רַבְרְבָֽן (phum memallil rabrevan) = "a mouth speaking great things"
- מְמַלִּ֥ל (memallil) = Verb.pael.Ptcp.ms "speaking" -- Pael = intensive/great speech
NOTE: Three different verbs for the horn removing three kings: (1) 'aqar (7:8, Etpeel "were uprooted" = passive); (2) nephal (7:20, Peal "fell" before it); (3) hashpil (7:24, Haphel "will bring low" = causative). The verb escalation: passive uprooting -> active falling -> causative subduing.

docs.title: Daniel 7:12 -- lives prolonged
docs.text:
וּשְׁאָר֙ חֵֽיוָתָ֔א הֶעְדִּ֖יו שָׁלְטָנְהֹ֑ון וְאַרְכָ֧ה בְחַיִּ֛ין יְהִ֥יבַת לְהֹ֖ון עַד־זְמַ֥ן וְעִדָּֽן

Key parsing:
- שְׁאָר (she'ar) = Noun.ms.Cst "rest/remainder" -- the rest of the beasts
- הֶעְדִּ֖יו (he'ddiyu) = Verb.haf.Perf.3mp of עדה ('adah) = "were removed" (Haphel causative passive)
- שָׁלְטָנְהֹ֑ון (sholtanehon) = Noun.ms.Abs+3mp "their dominion"
- אַרְכָ֧ה (arkah) = Noun.fs.Abs "prolongation/extension"
- בְחַיִּ֛ין (bechayyin) = Prep+Noun.mp "in/of life"
- יְהִ֥יבַת (yehibat) = Verb.peil.Perf.3fs "was given" -- passive = divine act
- זְמַ֥ן (zeman) = Noun.ms.Abs "time"
- עִדָּֽן ('iddan) = Noun.ms.Abs "time/year"
NOTE: Their DOMINION was removed but their LIVES were prolonged. This explains Rev 13:2 composite beast: earlier empires lost political dominance but their cultural/institutional DNA persisted and was absorbed by successors. The divine passive (yehibat) indicates God's sovereign control over their survival.

docs.title: Daniel 7:20 -- nephal (fall)
docs.text:
וְאָחֳרִי֙ דִּ֣י סִלְקַ֔ת וּנְפַ֥לָה מִן־קֳדָמַ֖הּ תְּלָ֑ת

Key parsing:
- נְפַ֥לָה (nepalah) = Verb.peal.Perf.3fp of נפל (nephal) = "fell"
- חֶזְוַ֖הּ רַ֥ב מִן־חַבְרָתַֽהּ (chezwah rab min-chavratah) = "its appearance greater than its companions"
NOTE: nephal (Peal Perfect 3fp) = "fell" -- active falling. This is the second of three uprooting verbs. The horn's "appearance greater than its companions" indicates a claim to greater authority than the ten.

docs.title: Daniel 7:24 -- yehasphil (bring low)
docs.text:
וּתְלָתָ֥ה מַלְכִ֖ין יְהַשְׁפִּֽל

Key parsing:
- יִשְׁנֵא֙ (yishneh) = Verb.peal.Impf.3ms of שׁנה (shanah) = "be different" -- diverse from the first
- יְהַשְׁפִּֽל (yehasphil) = Verb.haf.Impf.3ms of שׁפל (shaphal) = "bring low/subdue"
NOTE: yehasphil (Haphel imperfect) = "will bring low/subdue" -- causative + ongoing. This is the third verb (angel's interpretation): the horn WILL subdue three kings. The Haphel imperfect indicates ongoing action, not a single past event. yishneh ("be different") uses the same root shanah that appears in 7:25 lehashnayyah ("to change").

docs.title: Daniel 2:39 -- batarakh succession markers
docs.text:
וּבָתְרָ֗ךְ תְּק֛וּם מַלְכ֥וּ אָחֳרִ֖י ... וּמַלְכ֨וּ תְלִיתָאָ֤ה

Key parsing:
- בָתְרָ֗ךְ (batrakh) = Noun.ms.Abs+2ms "after you" -- from באתר (baatar) = "after"
- תְּק֛וּם (tequm) = Verb.peal.Impf.3fs "will arise"
- מַלְכ֥וּ (malku) = Noun.fs.Abs "kingdom"
- אָחֳרִ֖י (ochorey) = Adj.fs.Abs "another"
- אֲרַ֣עא (ar'a) = Noun.fs.Abs "earth" -- "inferior to you" (lit. "earthward from you")
- תְלִיתָאָ֤ה (telita'ah) = Adj.fs.Abs "third" -- explicitly numbered
NOTE: u-vatrakh ("and after you") establishes gap-free temporal succession. The third kingdom is numbered telitaya ("third"). These markers create an unbroken chain that does not permit gaps, rearrangement, or parenthetical insertions, directly countering the futurist gap thesis.

docs.title: Daniel 2:43 -- la lehevon dabqin (will not adhere)
docs.text:
וְלָֽא־לֶהֱוֹ֥ן דָּבְקִ֖ין דְּנָ֣ה עִם־דְּנָ֑ה

Key parsing:
- מִתְעָרְבִ֤ין (mit'arbin) = Verb.htpa.Ptcp.mp "mixing themselves" -- Hitpael = reflexive
- לֶהֱוֹן֙ (lehevon) = Verb.peal.Impf.3mp "they will be"
- בִּזְרַ֣ע אֲנָשָׁ֔א (bizera' anasha) = "in/with the seed of men"
- לָֽא (la) = Neg "not"
- דָּבְקִ֖ין (dabqin) = Verb.peal.Ptcp.mp of דבק (debaq) = "adhering/cleaving"
- דְּנָ֣ה עִם־דְּנָ֑ה (denah 'im denah) = "this with this"
- חֲסַ֣ף (chasaph) = Noun.ms.Cst "clay/ceramic"
- פַּרְזְלָא (parzela) = Noun.ms "iron"
NOTE: la lehevon dabqin = "they will NOT be adhering" -- a falsifiable prediction. Iron and clay mix (marriage alliances, political unions) but do not permanently fuse. This has been tested across 1500+ years: Charlemagne, Napoleon, Hitler, EU -- all failed to permanently reunify Europe's divided territory.

docs.title: Daniel 2:21 -- sovereignty hymn
docs.text:
מְהַשְׁנֵ֤א עִדָּנַיָּא֙ וְזִמְנַיָּ֔א מְהַעְדֵּ֥ה מַלְכִ֖ין וּמְהָקֵ֣ים מַלְכִ֑ין

Key parsing:
- מְהַשְׁנֵ֤א (mehashne) = Verb.haf.Ptcp.ms of שׁנה = "changing" -- Haphel (causative) Participle
- עִדָּנַיָּא֙ ('iddanayya) = Noun.mp "times" -- emphatic plural
- זִמְנַיָּ֔א (zimnanayya) = Noun.mp "seasons" -- emphatic plural
- מְהַעְדֵּ֥ה (meha'ddeh) = Verb.haf.Ptcp.ms of עדה = "removing" -- Haphel Participle
- מְהָקֵ֣ים (mehaqem) = Verb.haf.Ptcp.ms of קום = "setting up" -- Haphel Participle
NOTE: God is the one who mehashne (changes) times and seasons -- the SAME ROOT shanah that appears in Dan 7:25 where the horn lehashnayyah (thinks to change) times and law. God genuinely changes; the horn merely THINKS to (sbar = "intend"). The sovereignty hymn is the theological foundation for all four vision cycles.

docs.title: Daniel 9:27 -- gabar beriyth, la-rabbim
docs.text:
וְהִגְבִּ֥יר בְּרִ֛ית לָרַבִּ֖ים שָׁב֣וּעַ אֶחָ֑ד

Key parsing:
- הִגְבִּ֥יר (higbir) = Verb.Hiphil.Perf.3ms of גבר (gabar) = "make strong/prevail"
- בְּרִ֛ית (beriyth) = Noun.fs.Abs "covenant"
- לָרַבִּ֖ים (la-rabbim) = Prep+Art+Adj.mp "to/for the many"
- שָׁב֣וּעַ אֶחָ֑ד (shabua' echad) = "one week"
- יַשְׁבִּ֣ית (yashbith) = Verb.Hiphil.Impf.3ms of שׁבת (shabath) = "cause to cease"
- זֶ֣בַח (zebach) = Noun.ms "sacrifice"
- מִנְחָ֗ה (minchah) = Noun.fs "grain offering/present"
- כְּנַ֤ף (kenaph) = Noun.fs.Cst "wing" -- "upon the wing of abominations"
- שִׁקּוּצִים֙ (shiqqusim) = Noun.mp "abominations/idols"
- מְשֹׁמֵ֔ם (meshomem) = Verb.Piel.Ptcp.ms "desolating" -- the desolator
- נֶ֣חֱרָצָ֔ה (necheratsah) = Verb.Niphal.Ptcp.fs "decreed/determined"
- תִּתַּ֖ךְ (tittak) = Verb.Qal.Impf.3fs of נתך (nathak) = "be poured out"
NOTE: gabar beriyth (Hiphil = "make the covenant prevail/be strong") is deliberately NOT karath beriyth ("cut a covenant" = make NEW covenant). He STRENGTHENS/CONFIRMS the existing covenant. la-rabbim ("for the many") echoes Isa 53:11-12 "justify many" and "bare the sin of many" -- Messianic language. The subject of higbir is debated: HIST reads it as Messiah confirming God's covenant, supported by (1) la-rabbim Isaianic language, (2) gabar vs karath word choice, (3) the subject being "Messiah the Prince" from 9:25-26.

docs.title: Daniel 11:31 -- tamid + shiqquts vocabulary
docs.text:
וְהֵסִ֣ירוּ הַתָּמִ֔יד וְנָתְנ֖וּ הַשִּׁקּ֥וּץ מְשֹׁומֵֽם

Key parsing:
- זְרֹעִ֖ים (zero'im) = Noun.mp "arms" -- "arms from him shall stand"
- חִלְּל֞וּ (chillelu) = Verb.Piel.Perf.3p of חלל (chalal) = "profane/defile"
- הַמִּקְדָּ֤שׁ (hammikdash) = Art+Noun.ms "THE sanctuary"
- הַמָּעֹוז֙ (hamma'oz) = Art+Noun.ms "THE fortress/stronghold"
- הֵסִ֣ירוּ (hesiru) = Verb.Hiphil.Perf.3p of סור (sur) = "removed" (Hiphil causative)
- הַתָּמִ֔יד (hattamid) = Art+Noun.ms "THE continual" (= the daily)
- נָתְנ֖וּ (natenu) = Verb.Qal.Perf.3p of נתן (natan) = "placed/set up"
- הַשִּׁקּ֥וּץ (hashiqquts) = Art+Noun.ms "THE abomination"
- מְשֹׁומֵֽם (meshomem) = Verb.Piel.Ptcp.ms "desolating"
NOTE: Identical tamid + shiqquts vocabulary to Dan 8:11-13 and 12:11. Three chapters, one vocabulary, one power. The compound "sanctuary-fortress" (mikdash-ma'oz) is unique to 11:31.

docs.title: Daniel 12:11 -- tamid + shiqquts + time period
docs.text:
וּמֵעֵ֙ת֙ הוּסַ֣ר הַתָּמִ֔יד וְלָתֵ֖ת שִׁקּ֣וּץ שֹׁמֵ֑ם יָמִ֕ים אֶ֖לֶף מָאתַ֥יִם וְתִשְׁעִֽים

Key parsing:
- מֵעֵ֙ת֙ (me'eth) = Prep+Noun.s.Cst "from the time"
- הוּסַ֣ר (husar) = Verb.Hophal.Perf.3ms of סור = "was removed" (Hophal passive)
- הַתָּמִ֔יד (hattamid) = Art+Noun.ms "THE continual"
- לָתֵ֖ת (lateth) = Prep+Verb.Qal.InfCon of נתן = "to set up"
- שִׁקּ֣וּץ שֹׁמֵ֑ם (shiqquts shomem) = "the abomination that maketh desolate"
- יָמִ֕ים (yamim) = Noun.mp "days"
- אֶ֖לֶף מָאתַ֥יִם וְתִשְׁעִֽים (eleph matayim vetish'im) = "1290"
NOTE: Same tamid + shiqquts as 8:11-13 and 11:31. The 1290 days extends 30 beyond the 1260 (= time, times, half time). The Hophal passive husar ("was taken away") = divine passive, just as the tamid was divinely removed in judgment.

docs.title: H1855 - d'qaq (break in pieces)
docs.text:
• Transliteration: dᵉqaq
  • POS: verb
  • BLB Count: 10
  • Definition: (Aramaic) corresponding to; to crumble or (trans.) crush: break to pieces.
  • BDB: Pe. Perfect 3mp daquw Dan 2:35. Haph. break in pieces: Perfect 3fs haddeqet Dan 2:34,45; 3mp haddiquw Dan 6:24. Imperfect 3fs taddiq Dan 2:40 (absolute), Dan 2:44 (accusative); suffix taddᵉqinnah Dan 7:23; Participle active mehaddeq Dan 2:40 (accusative), feminine maddᵉqah Dan 7:7, Dan 7:19.
  • 13 total occurrences; translations: brake in pieces, breaketh in pieces, broken to pieces, etc.
  • KEY: Appears exclusively in Dan 2 (2:34,35,40,44,45) and Dan 7 (7:7,19,23) and Dan 6:24 -- binding chapters 2 and 7 together

docs.title: H8548 - tamid (continual/daily)
docs.text:
• Transliteration: tawmeed
  • POS: masculine noun
  • BLB Count: 104
  • Definition: from an unused root meaning to stretch; properly continuance; the regular (daily) sacrifice
  • 105 total occurrences; 53x "continually," 17x "the continual," 9x "continual," 7x "the daily"
  • Daniel occurrences: Dan 8:11, 8:12, 8:13, 11:31, 12:11 (all as "the daily")
  • KEY: Links Dan 8, 11, and 12 -- same power removes the tamid in all three contexts

docs.title: H6663 - tsadaq (be just/righteous/cleansed)
docs.text:
• Transliteration: tsaw-dak
  • POS: verb
  • BLB Count: 41
  • Definition: a primitive root; to be (causatively, make) right (in a moral or forensic sense): cleanse, clear self, (be, do) just(-ice, -ify, -ify self), (be turn to) righteous(-ness)
  • 54 total occurrences; Dan 8:14 is the ONLY Niphal occurrence, translated "be cleansed"
  • KEY: nitsdaq (Niphal) in Dan 8:14 is forensic, not ritual -- "be declared righteous/vindicated"

docs.title: H2852 - chathak (determine/cut off) -- HAPAX
docs.text:
• Transliteration: khaw-thak
  • POS: verb
  • BLB Count: 1
  • Definition: a primitive root; properly to cut off, i.e. (figuratively) to decree: determine
  • ONLY occurrence: Dan 9:24
  • KEY: Daniel used charats (H2782) 3x elsewhere for "determine" (Dan 9:26,27; 11:36). His deliberate choice of chathak (="cut off") in 9:24 is an authorial signal that the 70 weeks are "cut off" from a larger period (the 2300 days of Dan 8:14)

docs.title: H2782 - charats (decide/determine/decree)
docs.text:
• Transliteration: khaw-rats

  • BLB Count: 12
  • Definition: to point sharply; figuratively to be alert, to decide: bestir self, decide, decree, determine, maim, move
  • Daniel occurrences: Dan 9:26 ("determined"), Dan 9:27 ("determined"), Dan 11:36 ("determined")
  • KEY: Daniel's normal word for "determine" -- contrast with chathak (H2852) in Dan 9:24

docs.title: H5057 - nagiyd (prince/ruler/commander)
docs.text:

docs.title: H8269 - sar (prince/captain/chief)
docs.text:
• Transliteration: sar
  • POS: masculine noun

docs.title: H1080 - bela (wear out) -- HAPAX in Aramaic
docs.text:
• Transliteration: bel-aw

docs.title: H5732 - 'iddan (time/year)
docs.text:
• Transliteration: id-dawn
  • POS: masculine noun (Aramaic)
  • BLB Count: 13
  • Definition: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to that of; a set time; technically, a year: time
  • BDB: 1. in general, time as duration (Dan 2:8, 7:12). 2. definite time = year: "seven 'iddanin = seven years" (Dan 4:13,20,22,29); 'iddan we-'iddanin u-felag 'iddan (Dan 7:25, i.e. 3.5 years)
  • KEY: BDB explicitly glosses 'iddan = year in Dan 4. This establishes the day-year principle: if 'iddan = year in Dan 4 (literal), the same word in Dan 7:25 should also = year.
